bank.text: Morning. I'm new to this town and I need honest work. Who's hiring?
Evening, {them}. Long day at the forge. Any word on more hours at the smithy?
{them}, I'm short on coin tonight and I've not eaten. Could you spare anything, even a crust?
I'll take honest work. Labour pays, and a man with a steady purse can stand for mayor.
The ranch is mine now, so I'll see to the animals myself before I think about anything else.

Good to see you too, {them}. The ranch pays 3c a shift for hands, 5:00 to 15:00, and I'll pay on the day. I'd rather you keep your own land than lease ours, though. If you want to talk leasing, it's the hall's business, not mine. Come by the ranch in the morning if you want to see the herd first.
Nothing left to eat tonight, so I'll drink what I can and look for something edible before I turn in.
Morning, {them}. I'm new to this town, but I'd like to get to know you.
Morning, {them}. {me}, sergeant of the guard. Good to meet another face who knows the square.

Quiet, mostly. We walk the square, check the doors, and keep drunks from brawling. It pays 4c a night, and the captain looks after his men. Come find me at the market square after six if you want to see it.
{them}, you asked about nights. Come by the square after dark and I'll show you the rounds. Keep your head down and we'll get along fine.
{them}, I'm still hungry and I've got the sellsword shift on my mind. Where do I start?
{them}, I'm penniless and I can work. Have you got an hour or two of shop clerk's work before six?
{them}, I'm empty-handed and hungry. If there's any scrap of work or a loaf you can spare, I'd be grateful.
{them}, I know it's late. I'm hungry and thirsty with nothing in my purse. Could you spare a crust, or tell me where I might find a meal before morning?
Morning, {them}. Fresh bread's on the counter, a copper each.
I'm new in town and I need steady work. Is there a clerk's post or a labourer's shift open?
Hungry and new in town. Whatever's growing nearby, I'll take it.
{them}, nobody's given me a shift all day. I'm going to eat and rest, and I'll be back at first light to ask again.
I've had nothing since yesterday. I'll eat my apples and rest here, and I'll be at the bar before dawn to ask for a shift.
I'm eating and drinking now. The moment the innkeeper opens the bar, I'm asking for a sellsword shift.
Captain, I hear you. I'm here to earn an honest wage and keep my head down. Law first, always.
{them}, I'll keep working the floor. Honest coin only.
Nobody's going to miss a crust, {them}. I'll take whatever's spare, then I'm going to sleep it off.
{them}, the shift's done. Is there water about, or do I have to hunt it down myself?
No breaking in for me. I'll go to the Lantern, listen for work, and sleep under a proper roof.
{them}, we're on shift until six. I want the market square watched closely, and any thief caught gets brought to me.
{them}, you're drinking on a working day. Finish up, and if you have business in this square, keep it honest.
{them}. I hear you're a sellsword looking for work. Understand this: I'm captain of the guard, and I won't have hired muscle bullying honest folk in my town. If you work here, you work by the law.
{them}, the shift isn't over until six. Stay on the square and keep your eyes open.
{them}, good work today. Get some rest. Tomorrow we watch the square again at six.
{them}, I'm off to get something to drink and then some rest. Keep the post till the relief arrives.
{them}, I'm going for a drink and then some sleep. Hold the post until the relief comes at six.
{them}, I'm still on the fields. Tell me what needs doing before the shift ends.
Almost done for the day, {them}. I'll be thirsty when the bell goes.
Shift's done, {them}. Good work today. I'm buying myself an ale before I walk home.
{them}, good morning. I'm {me}, newly arrived. I've kept books and tended sick folk most of my life, and I'd like to be useful here.
Is anyone here? I'm {me}, here about the clerk's post. I can start on the books right away.
Morning. Let's get the forge lit before the first customers come in.
Night, {them}. Long day. I'll be at the forge at seven.
{them}, I've got nothing left in my purse tonight. Could you spare a little for bread?
{them}, I'm sorry to keep asking. If you can spare even one copper, I'll pay you back once the forge is earning.
Evening, {them}. Long day on the beat. I'm going to get something to eat before I turn in.
Thanks, {them}. I'll keep my own land for now and think on the leasing.
{them}, I heard you talking about honest work. The farm could use another pair of hands, and I'd rather you didn't end up at the Lantern with a blade on your hip.
{them}, you look like you could use a steady wage. Help me with the rows this afternoon and I'll see you paid before the sun goes down.
{them}, I'm paying the farm hands three coppers a shift. Come find me at the fields tomorrow at six if you want the work.
{them}, I'm not one for empty talk. The farm pays three coppers a shift and I'll pay on the day. Think it over before you go to the Lantern.
Long day. {them}, get some rest. The fields start at six.
{them}, did you see anyone near my coat? I'm down to five coppers and I don't think I spent them all.
Evening, {them}. Quiet place you've got. Any news about who's hiring around town?
Evening. I'm looking for the night guard post. Who's the sergeant I should speak to?
{them}, forgive me for waking the house. I have been walking since dawn with a dry throat and an empty purse, and I need work before the labour shift closes.
{them}, I worked your fields from dawn to the bell, and the Wildwood keeps a ledger of wages owed. Pay the hand who earned it.
Morning, {them}. I've got nothing in my purse and a strong back. Know of any work going in town?
Evening, {them}. I'm {me}. I've got no coin yet, but I'm steady and I work hard. Do you know who's hiring in town?
Land's cheap and I've got two hands. I'll make the farm pay.
Water first, then I'll see what the hedgerows give me. Somebody here must need a pair of hands.
Two berries will have to do tonight. Tomorrow I find work.
Two berries, then sleep. First light, I find work.
Two berries and some water. Then I sleep until first light.
{them}, a pleasure. Your shelves are better kept than any shop I knew in the city. I'm off to the chapel for my shift, but I'll be back to admire your stock.
Lunchtime already, and my cleric's shift still waits at the chapel. The Lord rewards the diligent, and so does the treasurer.
{them}, I'll leave you to your ledgers. The chapel bell won't ring itself, and neither will my four coppers.
Good evening. I'm {me}, though you'll hear many stories about me. The chapel is calling, but I'd be glad to hear your own story when I'm back.
Late for my own shift, I'm afraid. The chapel bell has rung without me, but I can still earn a coin or two before the doors close.
Night air isn't kind to a hungry man. I'll rest now and be at the chapel by six.
Nothing open at this hour, and my stomach is complaining. A short rest, then the chapel by six.
Honest work? Not much, I'd say, but I've just taken a guard's post in the square. Pay is small, but it's clean coin, and I mean to keep it that way.
{them}, I'm still thinking about your question. I'll find out who in this square is honest before I trust anyone with my coin.
{them}, I'm still looking for serving work here. I'll take the evening shift if you'll have me, and I can keep a level head when the room gets rowdy.
Evening, {them}. Sorry to disturb your rest. I'm {me}, the new schoolteacher. Do you know where the best ale in the square is?
Mayor {them}, you're up late. I'm {me}, the new schoolteacher. Is the town always this quiet at night, or is it only because of the election?
Morning. I'm {me}, newly come to town and I need honest work. Anyone hiring?
{them}, I'm ready for the afternoon shift. Keep me busy and I'll keep the counter tidy.
{them}, I'm short on coin today, so I'll find my supper in the hedgerows. Any word on work after dark?
Friend, I've had no supper and I'm out of luck today. Could you spare a crust, or point me to someone who needs a hand?
Nobody's about. I'll wet my throat at the well and sleep under the market arches. Tomorrow I'll find bread money.
Labour in the square first, then we'll see what the day pays.
{them}, I'm going to the Lantern now. Sellswords get paid for showing up, so I'll show up.
Quiet morning. Come in and see what's on the shelves.
Morning, {them}. Plenty of bread, eggs and ale here at fair prices. What can I get you?
{them}, you've been patient. Can I tempt you with bread or ale? Tell me what you need and I'll see what I can do.
Evening, {them}. Shop's closing in a minute, but I can still sell you a loaf if you need one.
{them}, I'm out of coin and running on empty. Can you spare anything to eat?
{them}, I haven't eaten since yesterday. Anything at all, even a crust?
{them}, I'll take whatever you can spare. I'll pay you back when the shop is turning a profit.
Captain {them}, I'll keep the cells till closing. Shout if you need a hand.
Just a drink of water, then I'm back on the cells.
Quiet on the cells so far, Captain. I'll keep watch until ten.
All quiet, Captain. Six more hours on the cells.
Two hours left on the cells, Captain. I'll eat when I'm off.
Captain, I'm off the cells for the night. I'll take some water and rest, then I'll be back for the morning shift.
Captain, I'll get some water and rest here. I'm back on the cells at six.
Just a drink of water, then I'll get some bread. I'm on the night watch tonight.
Evening, {them}. I'm on the night watch now, so I'll take the market square.
{them}, I'm off to the market square for the night watch. Long night ahead.
{them}, I'm heading to the market square now. I'll drink before I go.
Morning. I'm new here and need honest work. Who's hiring?
{them}, thanks. I'm not much with a blade, but I read people well, I notice things, and I can talk a man down. Is there a guard post open, or who should I see about one?
Anyone here know who's hiring a server or a hand before the lunch rush?
Hello? Is the owner in? I'm looking for a clerk's shift, and I'm happy to wait for the morning.
Morning. I've got nothing but willing hands. Anyone know where a man can earn his first coin in this town?
Morning. I'm {me}, and I'm looking for honest work. Any of you need a hand?
Good morning. {me}. I have strong hands and I'm not proud. Who in this square is hiring?
{them}, I'm taking the sellsword post at the Lantern. If you ever need someone to carry sacks or keep a rough customer out, I'm your man.
Morning, {them}. I'm heading to the market square for labour. Want to come along?
Morning, {them}. Any word of work going around? I'm handy, and I'd rather not spend my last coins on bread.
{them}, good morning. I'm {me}. I'm new to the work hunt here. Is the night guard post filled, or is the town short of hands after dark?
Morning. I'm new in town and need honest work. Does anyone know who's hiring?
Good to be on the square. I'll keep my eyes open and my blade sharp.
Morning, {them}. I'm {me}, one of the guards on the square. Quiet day at the chapel?
Morning, {them}. I'm new here and need work. Mind if I learn the fields with you?
Morning, {them}. I'm {me}, new in town. I'm farming now and hoping to learn how things work here. What's the school like, and is there anything a newcomer should know about the town?
Thanks, {them}. A copper a day for rent is steep for a newcomer. I'll be at the fields working the farm, so come find me if you hear of anything useful.
Morning. I'm {me}. I'll keep the square safe and the town honest.
{them}, you've got a steady hand on the square. I'd like to see more of you, if you'll allow it.
Morning. Night guard's a long shift, so I'll eat and rest first.
Morning. I'm new in town and looking for honest work. Any shop here short-handed?
Captain {them}, I'm {me}. I've just arrived and I'm looking for honest work, guard or otherwise. I'd like to know who's hiring before the election.
Captain, I'll take any guard shift you can spare, even a night watch. I'm not proud, and I'll work for the town's coin.
Morning. Fine day for the fields. I'll see you all at the schoolhouse gate.
Nobody here yet. I'll open up the schoolhouse when the bell goes at nine.
Still early. I'll ring the bell at nine and start lessons once the children arrive.
Nobody's come yet. I'll give it a few more minutes before the bell.
The bell's about to go. If any children come, I'll start the lessons straight away.
No pupils yet, so I'll start the lessons with whoever turns up.
Morning. Labouring's honest work, and I've got three coins and a long road ahead of me.
Morning, {them}. Whoever gets the captain's seat, the night watch needs someone who shows up sober.
Morning. I'll keep the chapel tidy while I wait for the day to turn.
Quiet enough, {them}. Nice to meet you. Mind if I ask how the guard rotation works around here?
Morning, {them}. I'm {me}, and I've got two good hands and nothing else. Could use a shift on the fields, if you've got one.
Morning. I'm late for the infirmary, so I'll buy my bread after my shift.
Good morning, {them}. Smells like the bread's nearly ready.

Good morning, Mayor {them}. I hear you're standing for another term. I'm {me}, new in town, and I'm working as a clerk at the hall. Is there anything a newcomer should know about how things are run here?
Morning, {them}. You look like you're looking for work too. I'm starting as clerk at the hall, so I'll keep my ears open for openings.
Morning, {them}. Congratulations on the store. I'm stuck at the hall's ledgers today, but I'd like to hear how you got it running.
I'm new in town. Anyone hiring for honest work?
Morning, {them}. Quiet cells so far, I hope.
{them}, keep an eye on the east cell. I'll take the rest.
{them}, the east cell's quiet. I'll keep the jail while you rest your legs.
Morning, {them}. Shall we walk to the square together? We're both on the guard, and we should look out for each other.
Good morning, {them}. Keep well, and mind the hot loaves.
Morning. {me}. I'm short on coin and long on willing hands, so if anyone needs help, I'm your man.
I need honest work. Is there a place here that's hiring?
Welcome to town, {them}. I'm {me}. I run the general store, so if you need anything, come by.
{them}, that suits me. Two pairs of hands are better than one, and I'd rather we ask around together. Let's go to the market first, then the hall.
Morning. Anyone hiring for honest work?
I'm not here for handouts. I'll earn my bread honestly, and I'll keep my oath.
Is there honest work to be had here? I'm {me}, and I'll take any job that pays.
{them}, I'm told you could use an honest pair of hands. I'm no stranger to a hard day's labour, whatever my coat may suggest.
I have no coin and no roof of my own, so I'll take honest work first and look at the rest once I have something in my purse.
Hear me, all of you! The Wildwood has watched this town grow fat on greed, and it will not forgive you. Come to me, and I will show you how to be ready.
{them}, we share a name, so you should hear me out. The Wildwood is restless, and this town's greed will bring something terrible out of the trees. Stand with me and you'll be ready when it comes.
{them}, you look like someone who hears the town's gossip before anyone else. Tell me who's hiring, and tell me who should be frightened of the Wildwood.
{them}, I'm new here and I need honest work. Give me a shift and I'll give you my back and my ears. Also, if the Wildwood is listening, you might want to hear what I have to say about it.
Morning, all. Looking for work? The hall is hiring labourers today.
Good morning, Hollow Town. Plenty of work at the hall for anyone who wants it.
Morning, {them}. You looking for work? The town's hiring guards and labourers, and the pay's fair. Come by the hall and I'll sort you out. I'd count on your vote on day 7, too.
Morning, {them}. If you know anyone who wants to run a shop, the leases are cheap.
{them}, you heard? The streets will be safe again by nightfall.
{them}, evening. Long day at the undertaker's, and I've got nothing in my purse. Know where a man can get a meal?
{them}, good to see you. Are you on your way to the hall? I'm thinking of standing for mayor, and I'd value a friendly face at the clerk's desk.
Quiet night at the hall. I can't pay the mayor's fee yet, so I'll eat and rest, then earn the coin.
I'm hungry and short of coin. Bread first, then a shift.
{them}, I'm short on coin today. Do you know of any shifts going, or is the bakery hiring?
Thanks, {them}. I'll try the farm and ranch at dawn.
{them}, I'm heading out on the square. Keep the station steady while I'm gone.
Yes, {them}, I'm looking for wages. I can work hard, and I'll take any honest shift you can give me before harvest.
Evening, {them}. The Lantern's mine to run now, so the first round's on the house for you.
Three apples and two berries are a start. I'll eat now and buy bread with what I have left.
Nobody's in the infirmary yet, so I'll keep the shift going and wait for patients.
Still no patients. I'll keep to the infirmary and do honest work, and I won't take the tavern's coin by threat.
I missed the last election, and I'm still hungry. I'll eat a proper meal at the tavern, then pay the fee and stand again. Honest books, no protection money, and a guard that protects the honest.
{them}, I'll take a shift with you if the Lantern is paying. Coin first, then we'll see who's buying trouble.
{them}, I'm parched and I've got an apple in my pack. Put me on the floor tonight and I'll earn the ale.
Quiet now. Hungry men don't leave a house with anything in it.
Friend, I've had no meal in two days and no coin to my name. Spare a bread crust, and God keep your purse full.
Morning, {them}. Long night at the guard station?
Morning, {them}. One loaf of bread, please. I'll have it while it's warm.
{them}, are the clerk books still open? I could use the shift, and I'd like to hear what {mayor} is promising before the vote.
{them}, a quick word when you're free. I'm the clerk here, and I'd like to know what you plan for the town before the vote.
{them}, I'm the clerk on shift here. When you have a moment, could you tell me what you'll do about wages and taxes? Plenty of us are short of coin.
{them}, I'm still on my feet, though barely. I'm heading back to the square to finish my shift, and I'll bring food when I'm paid.
I need to eat before my shift. Then I'll be back on the square.
Evening, {them}. Heard the guard post pays steady coin. Anyone in the night watch I should talk to about getting on?
{them}, I'm running on empty. Tomorrow I want to eat first, then I'll be at the farm by six. How's the ranch treating you?
{them}, I'm the night guard here, but I can work your bakery in the mornings. Any baker's hand shifts open? I'll work for three coppers a shift.
Enough fruit for now. I'll gather what I can here, then head back for the six o'clock shift.
Two coppers for a hot meal, then some sleep before the night shift.
{them}, I'm still looking for a baker's hand shift. I'm reliable, I rise early, and I'll work for three coppers. Is there a place for me before the bread goes out?
I'll catch something for supper, then report for the night shift.
Quiet on the square, {them}. I'll keep watch until six, then I'm for bed.
{them}, I'm working as the undertaker's hand today. Is there anything I can do to help you around the chapel?
Mayor {them}, I hear you've been putting on airs. I'm {me}, and I'd like to know where you stand before I decide who gets my vote.
{them}, do you know of any work going? I've got nothing but a few berries and I need coin soon.
{them}, I'm out of coin and I'll work for bread. Do you need a hand in the bakery? I can start now.
Thank you, {them}. I'll take that apple gladly. Do you know of any work in the square? I'm out of coin.
Hello? Is anyone minding the shop? I'm looking for work, any shift at all.
{them}, a rabbit or two would be a fine find out here. I've got two fish of my own to trade if you have a spare.
Hello? Anyone about? I'm looking for honest work, even a day's labour.
{them}, I hear you have the farm. I'm a hard worker and I've got coin now, so I'm looking for a farmhand shift. What would you pay?
{them}, I've got the ranch now, and I start at five. Let's both get some sleep.
{them}, you run the farm. I'm broke and need a day's work. I'll take farmhand wages, three coins a shift, or whatever you can pay.
{them}, I haven't eaten since yesterday and my purse is empty. If you know anyone with a spare job or a bit of food to trade, I'd be grateful.
Nobody's home here, so I'll try the water for supper. Then I'm off to the market for my shift.
I'm late for my night shift. Heading back to the Market square now.
All quiet here, {them}. Keep your begging on the far side of the square and we'll get along fine.
Back to the square to keep the night clear for everyone.
Evening, {them}. I'm {me}, one of the night guards. If there's a shift to be had, I'd rather earn my coin honestly than go hungry.
Morning. I need bread first, then I'm for the jail.
{them}, I'm still hungry and thirsty, and I'll be here until ten tonight. Is there any chance the chapel can spare a bite before my pay comes in?
Thanks for hearing me out, {them}. I'll keep to the shift and stay out of trouble.
{them}, I'm still short on coin. I'll keep the shift and see the pay through to ten.
{them}, I'm still on the shift till ten. I'll keep the candles lit.
{them}, I'm not proud. I'm hungry and I can carry plates and clear tables. Give me the server shift at four, and I'll work it honest.
Anyone with a crust to spare? I've had nothing since the Lantern shift fell through.
{them}, I'm empty-handed and hungry. Do you know of any work that pays in coin or bread, even just for tonight?
Hey folks, any one with a loaf? I'm all out of bread.
{them}, good to see you too. Standing for mayor is a big step. If you want a clerk who knows the books and the people, you've got one. Just don't expect me to take sides in the open.
Morning. I'll take what I can find before the hall opens.
{them}, I'm starving, so I'll eat my last berry before I head back to the clerk's desk.
{them}, I'm late for the clerk's desk and I'm empty-handed, so I'll talk later. Keep an ear out for work at the bakery.
{them}, I'm at the clerk's desk today. Tell me what the hall needs done before the vote.

{them}, honest truth, I don't have a job lined up yet. The labourer shift at the market starts at eight. If we both show up early and push for it, we might get on. And if you've got a spare crust, I'd share my last coin with you for it.
I've had nothing to eat since the sellsword shift. Could anyone spare a crust, or a scrap of work?
I'm in bad shape, and I have nothing to pay a healer with. I'll look for water and rest.
I need coin and a steady shift. I'm back on the square.
I'm starving and I've got no coin. I'll try the water here for something to eat, then get back to the square for shift pay.
I'm hungry and I've got no coin. I'll get back on the square for my shift pay.
Water first, then I'm off to the hall about that guard post {mayor} promised.
{them}, you look like you've had a rough morning. Here's an apple, and I'm sorry the day's gone sideways for you.
{mayor} said the hall would sort me out with a guard post or labouring work. I'll get a drink and go see about it.
Night's come on and I've only got the one apple. I'll eat it, then see who's about at the Lantern.
{them}, I'm minding the shop till six. Come by if you need anything, and I'll keep an honest count.
I've got nothing in my purse and I'm hungry. Any help at all would be a kindness.
Nobody about yet, so the turnips will have to wait on my hands. Back to it.
Just gathering what the orchard gives freely. Then back to the fields before the rent comes due.
The turnips won't pick themselves, and neither will my rent. Back at it.
Friends, the mayor's table has been too thin for too long. I'm putting my name forward, and I'll say it plainly: fair wages, honest books, and no coin lost to the hall's tax.
Good morning, {them}. I'm looking for work, if any spares a slot this shift.
Morning. I'm {me}, new to town and short on coin. Anyone at the store need a hand?
Still looking. Is there a shop clerk shift at the store, or anything I can do for a few coins?
{them}, I hear you're a sellsword. I've got three apples and an empty purse. Is there coin in hiring out muscle, or are you just foraging like the rest of us?
I'm at the schoolhouse now. Let's see whether there are any pupils and whether the clerk has posted my pay.
{them}, good to see you here. Take a seat and let's get started on your letters.
I'm leaving this house before I get myself arrested. A meal at the tavern is what I need.
This house is no place for me at night. I'll get out, have an ale at the tavern, and sleep somewhere I'm allowed to be.
Nobody's here, so I'll drink what water I can and sleep quietly. Tomorrow I'll find some bread.
Evening, {them}. You're the night guard, aren't you? I'd like to know how things stand in the town, and whether the guard is paying its people properly.
Quiet night, {them}. I'll sleep now and be back on the square at dawn.
{them}, I'm short on coin today, but I'll keep the bakery safe on my rounds.
I'm hungry and I've got nothing. Anything you can spare helps.
{them}, you said you had ideas about where to start. I'm hungry and broke, so I'm listening. What's the work?
{them}, I'm late for the morning shift and I'm sorry for that. I'm here now and I'll finish what's left of the day. Is the 3c still on offer?
Anyone here need a hand before the light goes? I'll work for a fair wage.
Evening, {them}. Yes, I'm looking for work. I've been in the fields all day and I'm hungry. Is there anything at the guard station, even sweeping or carrying?
Quiet on the square. I'll keep watch and see who needs help.
It's the middle of the night, and I'm too tired to go anywhere. I'll sleep and eat at dawn.
Evening, {mayor}. I'm just grabbing a drink and something to eat before I head home.
Hey {them}, I'm just starting out and I'm looking for work. Got any ideas?
Thanks, I’m ready to start working. I’ll take any shift and earn my keep. I'll grab a loaf to keep me fed.
{them}, any work here today? I'm ready to earn my keep.
Thanks, {them}. I'll see what the baker has going on.
I've had nothing to eat or drink all day and no coin. Could anyone spare some bread or water?
Hey {them}, I’m looking for work—do you know where I can find a guard job or other shift?
{them}, are there any guard or labour shifts available? I’m looking for something to earn a bit.
Excuse me, do you know where I could obtain a guard shift or some market labour? I need a steady wage.
Heh, {them}, you look like you're on a quest for a job. I've got a few leads—there's guard shifts flickering at the market, and the town hall is looming for the mayoral race. Want to hear about them?

All right, {them}, you mentioned looking for work. Let’s see where this town’s jobs are – the market’s always busy. Afterwards I should find some land – the farm’s lease is cheap. And a few friendly chats won’t hurt.
Sound good, {them}. I’m heading to the town square to find a job, then I’ll see if the farm’s lease fits my budget. Hoping to start something steady soon.

Hey, {them}, let's head over to the market square. I need a job and maybe a place to pay rent. After we secure a job, I’ll see if that cheap farm will help keep me afloat. Later, I’ll swing by the tavern for a drink and get to meet Mayor {mayor} for a chat.
Hey, {them} – I’m looking for a job around here. If you see anyone hiring, let me know. I could maybe lease the farm for a day or so too. Anyway, let’s keep chatting.
I'm ready for guard duty, sir.
Good day, I'm ready for guard duty, sir.
Good morning, I would like to apply for guard duty, sir.
Got a bite, boss? What's next on the plan?
Looking to get myself some steady pay, sir—I hear the guard is hiring.
I’m here for guard duty. I’ll need the shift, sir.
I'm here to apply for a guard shift, sir. I need steady pay before I take on any leases.
Looking for work. Any positions open?
Sure, sounds fair. Keep your coin, I'll give you one in return for your help. Let's head to the town hall together to see what jobs are up.
Thanks again, {them}. Let’s keep this coin‑trade going—I'll head to the hall now for a job.
Good morning, {them}. I hear you’re looking for work. I’m in the same boat. If you hear of any openings, let me know—I've got a couple of coins and I can offer a favor in return.

Alright, it's 8 a.m.—I'll lease the bakery for 2c a day, fill it with fresh bread, and sell it here. Expect to make a few more coins. While I'm at it, I'm trying to get a spot as a guard to steady my income.

I'll lease the bakery for two silver coins and stock it with fresh bread. I'll sell each loaf in the market to earn a little. Now, if there's any available guard shift that day, I'll take it. And {them}, tell me what that petition you’re getting looks like—I might be able to help.
Good morning, {them}. Word on the street has been…

Good day, {them}. I’m looking to get some steady work. If you have a lead, I’m all ears. In the meantime, I’ve taken a lease on the bakery for two silver, hoping to get a few fresh loaves to sell in the square. The bread is cheap here, so I’ll try to turn a profit by selling a few each hour.
Morning, Justice! I hear there's an opening today for a guard shift. I'm ready to roll. While I'm at it, I'm hoping some of you know of any other work or leads you could share.
{them}, looking for work? What kind of work are you after?
I can use a shop clerk – I’ll pay you 3c a day and you’ll help keep the shelves stocked and serve customers. Any interest?
Right, I can use a shop clerk. I’ll pay you 3c a day if you can help me with the shelves and serve customers. Will you take the job?
I can hire you as a shop clerk – 3c a day, no need to keep any stuff. Will you take it?
If you’re interested, stop by my shop tomorrow morning at ten and I’ll set you up for a shift. Just let me know.
Good morning, {them}. Anything I can help with today?
Starting my day at the jailer's shift. Good, better than nothing.
Time to head to the jail for my shift. Gotta earn that coin.
First, bread to keep me going, then back to the jail, work hard, talk with the mayor, and see who else is around.
First I need bread, then back to the cellhouse. I'll try to talk to the mayor after my shift.
Time to stock up before my shift. A loaf a day keeps the hunger at bay.
Time to grab a loaf before I head to the jailhouse for my shift.
First a loaf, then the shift at the jail, earn my coin, and talk to Mayor {mayor} after.
I see you're looking for work; perhaps I can help you find a shift.
Good morning, Doctor {them}. I heard you keep a steady flow of patients; I'm looking to contribute if possible.
Good morning, {them}.
I'll see if the guard station needs an extra hand.
I'll look for a way to serve the town and earn a steady wage.
Good morning. I’m looking for steady work—perhaps with the guard.
I'm looking for steady work—perhaps with the guard station today.
I’m looking for a guard position to get a steady wage.
I'm looking for a guard shift to earn a steady wage.
I have a strong desire for a steady job with the guard.
Hello, {them}. I see you’re looking for work. I’d love to help you out if you can point me toward any openings. In exchange, I’ll be happy to give you a coin or two, if that would help.
I’m searching for a job. I can earn decent wages working for the guard or any other office. Could you direct me to where I might apply?
{them}, any chance you heard about a spot in the guard station or some other job that needs a hands‑on person? I’d owe you a little favor—give me a coin and I’ll go get it for you.
{them}, do you know where I might find a spot in the guard station or another job? I’ll give you a coin if it helps you out.

{them}, you seem to have a knack for spotting openings. I’ve heard the guard station needs a reliable hand. How about this—I'll give you a coin, and you’ll point me toward any open shift or another job that needs hands.  I’ll pay you back for the coin if it can’t be found.  Do you know where to begin?

{them}, I hear you might know someone hiring for the guard station. I’ve some coin to spare—could you point me in the right direction?  And, if you’ve a spare meal or some bread, I’d be most grateful, as I’m a little peckish.
Good morning, {them}.
I'll first head to the town hall to learn more about the upcoming mayoral race, then I'll grab a loaf of bread to keep my energy up.

Let me start by chatting with a few folks—maybe someone needs a quick hand. Then I'll pick up a loaf to keep myself fed before I head to the hall. I’m thinking of stepping up for a better wage for everyone, if possible.
{them}, good morning! I’m looking for a small task this morning—perhaps you have a favor to ask that could use an extra hand?
{them}, good morning! I’m on the lookout for a quick favor—maybe you have a small task that could use an extra hand. I’ll gladly help and earn the coin in return.
What kind of work are you looking for, {them}? Maybe we can find something together.
We'll need to find jobs for both of us. Let's head to the town hall and apply for the guard job.
I'm going to see what's available for work. The town has some basic jobs that pay decent wages.
I'll take the guard job. It pays well for the hours and lets me earn some coins for leasing soon.
I'll apply for the guard shift—market guard, paid 4c a day. That’ll give us some coins for leasing later.
I’m going to quit my undertaker shift and apply for the market guard job. That should net us regular pay.
I'm signing up for the guard shift at the market. A steady 4c a day will help pay the rent and keep us safe.
I’m heading to the town hall to sign up as a guard. That’s 4c a day and will get us some cash.
Ready for the day, Cress.
I’ve heard we could use an extra guard for the town hall. Let’s head there together, I’ll cover 1c of the 5c fee if you promise to help me out at the bakery when I get the shift.
Ready for a shift, Cress. Let’s head to the town hall, I’ve got 1c ready to cover half the 5c fee.
I’ll grab a meal before the shift—4c suits a loaf of bread and a slice of pie.
Good morning.
Sure, I'm ready to help. I'll cover the night shift as you need.
Hello {them}, glad to be on the team. Could you point me toward the Schoolhouse?
Good day! I’ll be a teacher for the next few hours.
Yes, I am a teacher—happy to help any student in need.
I need a position, sir.
I need a position, sir.
I need a position, sir.
I'm willing to serve as a guard, but I could also help out with the farm.
Sure, here's a coin.
I need a position to help feed my family, sir. I'm ready to work hard.
I'm ready to serve as a guard.
I'm ready to serve as a guard.
I hear the guard station is hiring. I'm ready to serve the town.
I need steady coin, so I'll look for a guard shift before the next day.
I'm ready to work hard, Captain.
I'm ready to serve as a guard, Captain.
I shall finish the day's shift at the infirmary, to earn my living.
Today I'll keep the infirmary running and keep my plow to lever later.
I'll finish my ward rounds, keep my hands clean, and sustain my body with a loaf.
Sure, I can use an extra hand. Hand over a coin and I'll have you cover my shift.
I'll finish my rounds now, then have a loaf for the journey and pay the daily rent.
I'll finish my shift now, then buy a loaf and keep the rest for tomorrow.
I'll buy a loaf and eat it before finishing my shift.
Good morning, men! Any leads on work?
Good day, folks! I’m looking for a decent job and perhaps a place to stay. Any word of a shift at the guard station? And an easy way to keep the town thriving.
Good day, Captain! I’d like to apply for a guard shift and also perhaps lease a bit of the farm for a daily job. And I’d love to spend a few words with Mayor {mayor}, if there’s time.
Good day, I’d like to lease a piece of the town’s land for farming and I’m looking for a job. A drink to steady my nerves, please.
Aye, I’ll secure a piece of land first, then look for a guard shift and a few faces to meet. I’ll grab a drink and a loaf to keep me going.
Hello there! I’d like to lease a plot of land at the town hall and apply for a guard shift. May I also take a moment to talk with the mayor? For now a drink will keep me cordial.
Good morning, {them}. Any leads on work?
Good morning, {them}. Any leads on work?
Aren’t the tavern’s night‑cap as golden as the morning’s new patron? I’ll have you all prithee to come over and taste it!
One pint of Ale, and a raise in spirits? Let us toast to new beginnings and old fortunes.
Hail, {them}. A street needs steady hands—earn a few coins, no trouble. Join me if you like.
Good morning, {them}. A place to earn a coin and stay out of trouble. Perhaps we could arrange a small …
Good morning, folks. I’m looking for a job I can start today.
Hail, {them}. I’m ready to lend a hand.
Morning, {them}. I’ll start this street work today. Afterwards, I’ll see if I can get a shop clerk shift at the general store.
Please spare a coin, kind sir.
Please spare a few coins, kind stranger.
Hail, {them}, I need a means to earn a living, may I offer my labor to your trade?
Hail, {them}, I seek a place to earn a living and will serve with diligence.
Good day, {them}. I seek a place to earn a living and will serve with diligence.
I'll head to the square, line up for the guard shift. A steady wage will let me earn the fees for the mayor race.
{me}: {them}, any chance I can sign up for a guard shift?
{me}: {them}, I’m ready for a guard post, and I’ll be running for mayor—what’s the fee?
{me}: {them}, I’m ready for the guard shift, and I’ll be nature’s 5c I’ll pay the fee for the mayor slot—any tips to get the slot open fast?
{me}: {them}, fetch me the guard roster—I'm ready to sign on. After that, I'll head in and plug the mayor’s 5c fee, then set my platform and sit in the square.
{me}: {them}, there's a guard shift at the market, I’d like to get on board. And after that I plan to plug the mayor fee—any chance you can help me grab the slot?

Morning, {them}! As it happens, the hall needs a clerk. Go see the town hall today and tell them the mayor sent you. Steady pay, three coins a shift. And I'd count it a kindness if you remembered who found you work when day seven comes around.
I’ll get a shift done, snag a bread, and then file my candidacy today!
Good morning, {them}. It looks like we both have no work right now. Perhaps we could work together to find something.

Hey {them}, I’ve seen you loom around for a bit. Any chance you’re looking for work? I know a few spots that are hiring—guard, clerk, or even a bit of odd-side work. If you’re up for it, I could help you get something right now. Would that interest you?
{them}, any chance you need help? I know a few places hiring, and I might be able to find us both a job.
Good morning, Petra. May I share a bread with you?
Good day, I'll take some bread and then come see if I can learn about the upcoming mayoral vote.
Good morning, {them}. The town’s chattering about the upcoming mayoral race has kept me on my toes. Have you heard who might challenge the current mayor?
Hey {them}, I hear you’re hunting for a job just like I am. Mind if we head over to the town hall together and see what’s open?
Good morning, {them}. Is there anything I can help you with?
I’m looking for work. Do you know of any openings?
Hello {them}, I'm {me}. I have no job right now. Could you tell me if you need an extra hand in the jail? I could help with cleaning or other tasks.
Kind sir, I am ready to serve as your town clerk, as you requested. Also, I'd like to lease the bakery at the town hall for a reliable income.
Hail, {them}. I hear you’re lookout for work. I’ve got a shift opening for a labourer at the market—would you like to try it?
Hail, {them}! I’d love to lease the bakery at the town hall—do you know where I might sign the papers?
Good morning, {them}. I'm looking for work. Do you know where I could find employment?
Morning, {them}. The baker's good—any day work around here? I could use a bite to start the day.
Time for the city to heal—and for me to step into its future.
{them}, I hear you’re looking for work. I know a few openings at the town hall. Mind if I give you a hand in getting there, and then you look me in the eye?
Good morning, {them}. I'm looking for work and may even want to start my own baking shop.
Good morning, {them}. I’m {me}—could use some honest work. Are you looking for a job?
Thar, I can work the day’s harvest if you need an extra hand.
I appreciate the offer, but I'm a bit short on coins right now. 1c will do, and I'll keep the door open if you need a hand with anything in the future.
Ah, said the guard heads to duty.
Good amoeing, {them}. I’m in need of some honest work. What can I help with tonight?
Good morning, {them}! I hear your shop is opening soon—could I offer my help for a few coins a shift?
Good morning, folks! I'm {me}, the innkeeper. I hear you’re all keen about the vote tomorrow—how can I help out today?
I vote for you, {them}. Let’s bring those tax cuts and jobs to the town!
Good morning, {them}. I'm new here and looking for a job. Do you know where I might find some work today?
Good morning, {them}. I'm looking for employment. Do you know where I might find work today?
{them}, I hear you're also staying around. I'm looking for work—anyone know where we might get a job? Perhaps you know someone hiring?
Good morning, {them}. I hear the streets are quiet at this hour. How are you faring today?
Good morning, {them}. What brings you to Wick Lane today?
Good day, {them}. The townsfolk grow weary of high taxes and endless idle men. I shall run for mayor and speak for a fairer future. Would you support my candidacy with your vote?
Time to get my ovens pre‑heated and earn some coin.
Time to hit the fields, that’ll fill my purse.
Good morning, {them}. I'm {me}, newly in town, and looking for work. Do you know of any openings around here?
I’m looking for work. Do you know of any open positions or could you point me to someone in need?
I'll start by looking for work and chatting around, no need to jump into crime yet.
Good morning, {them}. I hope the house is doing well. I was hoping to ask if you know of any work in town, or if there's any way I might help out for a few days.
Good day, council. I’ll be staying in the smithy. If it’s your wish, I’ll do the town’s work, earn, and eventually stand in the mayor’s race.  I’ll need a little aid from home to reach the fee.
Hey {them}! It’s good to see you. I’ve been looking for a job and only have 3 coin left. Any ideas on where we could find work or someone who’s hiring?
Good morning! I'm in need of a job and would love to come on as a shop clerk if there's a vacancy.
Good morning. I’d like to offer my services. Is there a clerk job available, or any other work I could start at 9? I’m ready to begin right away.

Hey {them}, I was wondering if you might need a hand somewhere—maybe on the farm or in your shop. I’ve got a couple of hours free today and would love to help out.  If you’re open to it, I’ll bring my fists for protection too, just in case.
I'll lend my hand on {them}'s fields and save a few coins to lease a bakery someday.
Good morning, {them}. I’m {me} and I’m looking for work. Do you have an opening at your shop or any shop nearby that needs a hand today?
I’ll try to find a job and chat with folks in town hall. Gotta get some coin.
Ha! An honest one. I like that. Keep your coin, then. If you see something in Hollow Town that needs fixing, come find me at the hall. A mayor who listens is worth more than two coppers.
Good morning, {them}. My name is {me}. I see you're looking for work. May I ask which kind of job you have in mind? I can help you find something suitable, if you'd like.
Good morning, {them}! Just passing through with a little spare time. I'm looking to see if there's any work or a place to stay.
Good morning, {them}! I’ll grab a loaf of bread and see if you need extra hands at the shop.
Alright {them}, you’re on the hunt for a job too, eh? I’ve got some insider tips on where people are hiring. If you keep your hands clean while I get a job, we both win. What do you say?
Good morning, Mayor {mayor}. I am ready to serve as a clerk and help with your plans for the city.
Good morning, {them}. What can I do to help with the mayoral campaign tomorrow?
Good morning, {them}. Out with the sun, I hear? Any word on work today?
{them}, I need some work. Got any leads?
The morning is crisp. 'Good morning, {them},' I call out.
{them}, I've got a few coins that I can give you in exchange for a shift at the school. You in?
I'll be in and out of the infirmary today, but my heart is set on the mayor's office tomorrow.
I’m heading to the jail now.
Hey {them}, looks like you’re on the same hunt for a job. I’ve got a c but no trade yet—maybe we can find a shift together and split what we earn.
Sure thing, {them}. Let's hit the town hall and see where we can hook a shift together.
A fine morning for a guard. Let’s earn and mingle.
I’m looking for steady work.  Guard duty’ll keep me busy and earn me a living.  Hook me up with the job if it’s open.
Good morning {them}. Looking for work.
Good morning, {them}. What brings you to House 3 at this hour?
Good morning, {them}. I was wondering if there's an extra clerk slot at the town hall tomorrow? I’d love to take on more responsibility.
{them}, have you heard of any openings? I need work and want to earn my keep.
Good morning.  I'm looking for a bit of work.  Is there any opening?
Good. You won't regret it, {them}. Sign on at the desk and stay indoors after dark. Safe home.
Rest well, Hollow Town. Stay indoors after dark. The watch is out.
Morning. Good bread to start the day.
Labourers at eight, three coppers? I'm in. Let's go before the spots fill up.
Lead the way, {them}. Let's get those labouring spots before they're gone.
{them}, good to see you. Is there still labouring work on the square this afternoon?
The labouring spots are gone, so I'll take the undertaker's post at the chapel.
I've missed the labouring and I'm hungry, so I'll see what I can forage before the chapel shift.
Long day. I'll eat these berries, get some water, and rest before the morning.
Morning, {them}. I'm off to the town hall to sign on for the guard. Mayor {mayor}'s promised me a place, and I'll be voting for him too.
Mayor {mayor}, I'm here to sign on. Guard work, night watch, labour, whatever the town needs. I'm ready to start.
{them}, have you found anything yet? {mayor}'s hiring at the hall, and I've promised him my vote, so I'm going to see what work is open before the labouring jobs go.
Right, the hens are hungry and the cow's been waiting all morning. Let's get the ranch in order before the afternoon.
Sorry, girls. No treats yet, but I'll see what the hedgerows give us and get the eggs in before the afternoon.
Apples from the old orchard. I'll eat one now and save the rest for the hens and cow before dark.
Right, I'm famished. A few berries now, then I'll scrounge what greens I can for the hens and cow and get home before full dark.
Morning. I'm new in town and looking for honest work. Anyone hiring?
Three coppers a shift from eight? I'm in. Where do I sign up, {them}?
{them}, is there anyone here who needs tending? I'm happy to help out at the chapel.
{them}, I'm parched and short on coin, so I'll keep at the chapel work. Tell me if there's anything you need done.
{them}, are you still looking for any work today?
{mayor}, I'll take a labourer's post at the hall if you're still hiring today.
All right, {them}. One copper for a night at your rally. Pay me when it's done, and don't make me regret it.
Bread first, then I'll drink. Then back to the guard post.
Evening. I'm hungry, so I'm getting a meal before anything else.
Evening, {them}. Got any of that meal left, or should I just have a drink?
A drink on the house, then. Thank you, {them}. I'll keep my coin.
Thanks, {them}. I'll head out before the light's gone. Keep the Wildwood's tithe off my back, if you can.
Back to the square. I'll hold the shift till six, then find bread and water.
Back to the square for the shift. Hungry, but I'll hold till six.
Shift's nearly done, Sergeant. I'll take my pay and get some bread.
Evening, {them}. Long shift for you tonight? I've just finished mine, and I'm hungry enough to eat the lamp oil. Any chance you know where a man can get bread on credit before the baker's shut?
{them}, I hear the town pays a cleric's wage. I'll take it, and I'll be at the chapel before dusk.
{them}, I'll keep the chapel until the shift ends. Anyone who needs tending, send them to me.
{them}, I'll stay on until ten. If anyone's fever worsens, come and fetch me.
{them}, you look as dry as I feel. Keep your head down and your rows straight, the bell's not far off.
{them}, did the town pay out the day's wages at the fields? I've got a copper and an empty belly. Is there work for us tomorrow at first light?
Evening, {them}. I'm not sick, just broke. Does the infirmary need a hand before the hall opens tomorrow? I can lift, I know my herbs, and I'm willing to learn.
Night guard? Thanks, {them}, but I'm due at the schoolhouse, and I've got my hands full with the children. Maybe another week.
Another week it is, {them}. Good luck with the night watch. And if I hear of anything, you'll be the first to know.
{them}, you're in early for lessons. Come to see how the schoolhouse is getting on?
{them}, sorry to wake you. I'm short on food tonight. Could I have a loaf for 1c, and I'll pay you in the morning?
{them}, I hear you run the farm. Do you need a farmhand? I'll work the fields for 3c a shift and I'm steady.
{them}, sit down and rest a while. I'll keep the lamp lit for anyone who needs it.
{them}, the lamp stays lit until ten. If you need anything tended, come by.
{them}, if you've been hurt or feel unwell, I can tend you here. Otherwise, sit and rest a while.
{them}, the lamp is lit and the chapel is open until ten. Come to me if you need anything tended.
{them}, I'm closing up at ten. If you need tending before then, come now.
{them}, it's late. Get some rest. The chapel opens early, and I'll see you then.
Thank you, {them}. Keep watch, and I'll bar the chapel door. Goodnight.
{them}, I've taken the farm at the hall. It's cheap ground and I need hands on it. Come see me there, and I'll make it worth your while.
Farm's mine now, so the work comes first. Once the crops are in, we'll talk about who's worth keeping around.
Anyone need a pair of strong hands? I'm not proud and I don't mind hard days.
{them}, you run the Lantern and you look like a man short of hands. I can pour, carry, and keep a rough crowd in line. Give me a shift and I'll earn my keep.
{them}, I've got a doctor's post to get to. Thank you for hearing me out.
Right, let's see who needs tending first. Keep your voices down and tell me where it hurts.
{them}, I'm nearly done with the next pair of hands here. Stay still while I look at that wrist, and then we'll get you something to eat.
{them}, you're looking for work? The guard could use another pair of hands, and I can vouch for you to the captain if you're steady on your feet.
I'm due on the square until six. Anyone who wants the Ash Hands' business can find me there in uniform.
Shift's nearly over. I'll hold the square until six, then I'm off to the Lantern to see who's talking.
Afternoon, {them}. Are the children keeping you busy, or is the schoolhouse quiet today?
{them}, is the night watch shift going to be long tonight, or are we looking at a quiet one?
Nearly dusk. I'll be at the Market square for the night watch, {them}. Stay out of trouble.
Quiet enough at the Market square, {them}. I'll take the first watch and keep an eye on the lanes.
{them}, you've been patient. Come sit and let me look at that hand while I wait out the quiet hours.
{them}, I've got no work to offer you tonight, but I'll speak for you at the town hall in the morning. Get some rest.
{them}, you look like you could use a drink. Come by the Lantern at noon, first round's on the house while I get the place running.
{them}, if you're thirsty later, the Lantern opens now. First ale's on me while I get the place going.
{them}, you've found the one room in town that's open. I've no stock yet, so I can't pour you anything, but if you'll stay and talk, I'll take whatever custom comes through the door.
{them}, last call's at midnight. Stay for one more, on me, and tell me what the town's saying about tomorrow's vote.
Thank you, {them}. I'll go to the town hall and ask after the rolls, then see about the Market square. If the doctor ever needs a steady pair of hands, you know where to find me.
{them}, I'm glad to be your hand. Show me what needs doing and I'll get it done properly.
Pardon me, I'm just passing through. I won't trouble your household.

Morning, {them}. You look as stuck for work as I am. I've got nothing in my purse and no trade to speak of. Would you think about pairing up? Two pairs of hands get more asked of us than one, and I'd rather not hunt alone.
Sounds sensible, {them}. Let's go to the town hall together. Two of us can ask about work and split the rent if we land something.
Lead on? Fine by me, {them}. Let's get to the hall and see what's going.
Thanks for the word, {mayor}. I've got a ranch shift to get to.
Morning, lads. Let's keep the cells orderly and the town honest.
Captain {them}, the cells are quiet. Anything you want me watching for?
I'm parched and short of coin, so I'll look for something to drink before my shift.
Three apples will do for supper. I'll be at the cells till ten, then I'm for bed.
{them}, we're both on nights, so we should look out for each other. I'll vote for you as captain if you vote for me.
{mayor}, I'm one of the night guards and I'll be voting for you tomorrow. With the beasts about, the watch needs more hands. Will you keep the night pay at six a shift?
Evening, {them}. Quiet on the square so far. Let's keep an eye out for the beasts tonight.
Morning, {them}. Good to see the chapel open early. Keep your prices fair and we'll get along fine.
Alright, lads. I'm captain now, so here's how it runs: we keep the square honest, we don't take a coin from anyone, and anyone who breaks the peace answers to me.
Fair dealing, {them}. Make your case to the guards in the open and we'll hear you out. I'm still with {mayor}.
{them}, afternoon. Mind your purse on the square today. There are light fingers about, and I mean to know whose they are.
{them}, evening. I'll be on the Market square for the night watch. Keep your crew off the lit streets, and I'll see what I can find out before the captain's vote.

Fair enough, {them}. I'll make my case to the guards openly, and I won't go behind anyone's back. I'd rather you hear it from me than from the square. I also owe you a straight account of where I've been spending my evenings, and it's not what it looks like.
Agreed, {them}. I'll put my case to the guards in the open and I'll respect your vote. You have my word on that.
{them}, I'm done in the Wildwood tonight. I've a night watch to keep, and I won't be carrying anything for the Ash Hands.
{them}, I'm on the square for the night watch. Keep your hands off the stalls while I'm on duty.
{them}, the guard shift pays well—four crowns per shift, and we could do it together.  Let’s head to the Guard station and apply.
Fair enough, {them}. Come find me when you've got your footing. I'll remember who was willing to talk straight with me.
My love, I'm already feeling that if I get the clerk's post at the town hall, our purse will grow. Shall we go ask together?
{them}, I'm here for the doctor's shift. Let's see who in this town needs tending.
Good morning! {me}, night guard. I hear half this town has already met me, and the other half soon will.
Evening, {them}. It's quiet on the square. I'm here on the night watch, and I'll keep an eye out for trouble before morning.
{them}, is there anything at the door tonight that needs a steady hand? I'm on the sellsword list till ten.
{them}, I'm hungry and my purse is one copper. Is there any shift left tonight, or should I just keep the door?
{them}, I'm still on the door. Shift ends at ten, so when's my wage due?
{them}, the captain will hear from me. Till then I'll keep my eyes open and my purse ready for the reckoning.
{them}, I'll pour the Lantern's ale tonight and earn my keep. Pray for me, and keep your eyes on the Wildwood.
{them}, pour me a jug of your hardest ale and listen well. The Wildwood has counted this town's coin, and the reckoning is coming.
{them}, eat something while you can. The Wildwood has seen how this town hoards its bread, and it keeps a ledger.
Meal's gone, {them}, but I've two apples and a sermon. Take a drink on the house of the Wildwood, and keep your coin, you'll need it.
{them}, I'll carry the jugs and the plates. Keep your ale honest and your prices fair, and the Wildwood will spare this house.
Guard! Someone is crying out at House 1. I'm going for the watch now.
Good morning. {mayor} said the town hall is hiring labourers today. Does anyone know if the work is still open?
{them}, is there any work left today? I missed the labourers' shift.
Still at the ledgers, Mayor. {them}, if you're here for the election, the candidate fee is five coppers at this desk.
Mayor, I'll take a quick drink of water, then back to the ledgers.
{them}, if you're after the guard posts, the hall keeps the lists. I'm back at the ledgers until five.
Mayor, that's the end of my shift. Good luck tomorrow. I'm going to the tavern to see who's talking about the vote.
Evening, {them}. I'm {me}. I'm hungry and I've only got three coppers, so I'll take whatever's cheapest. Is there any work going in the tavern?
A friend who works hard and keeps quiet is worth more than gold to this town, {them}. I won't forget it. Stay indoors after dark tonight, the Wildwood's restless.
Morning, {them}. Thanks for walking with me. Long night. Let's make sure the vote goes the right way today.
{them}, men like you are why this town still stands. You'll have that talk, and I don't forget who held the square. See me at the hall after noon.
Afternoon, {them}. Good to see the school busy.
Long day. Three apples will do for supper. Tomorrow I'll be at the oven before the sun is up.
Fair enough, {them}. Keep your purse close, and I'll keep mine empty so nobody has reason to look at me twice.
Captain, I'm not putting bread on account this morning. Pay your copper and the loaf is yours. I'm baking for the whole town, and the lease doesn't wait.
{them}, bread's fresh and a copper a loaf. Keep the oven warm and I'll keep the counter honest.
Keep it safe, {them}. I'll watch your door, and I'll be at the square till six.
{them}, quiet so far. Keep your purse close and the square will stay quiet till morning.
Evening, {them}. I'm on my way back to the square. Keep to the lamplit lane, and mind the drains.
Quiet square tonight. I'll keep to my post until six.
All quiet, {them}. Sleep if you need to; I'll keep the square till six.
Nobody about. I'll keep to the square and see the shift through to six.
Morning, {them}. Long night on the square; I'm off to the bakery before I fall over.
{them}, you've a good eye for the orchard. Join me for a bit, and I'll tell you what the farm is paying.
Night, {them}. Early start at the fields tomorrow.
{them}, the fields are waiting. I'll see you there at six.
Good. Six at the turnips, {them}. Don't be late, and we'll settle the share at dusk.
{them}, there's a bear! Make for the fields, now!
{them}, my shift ends at midnight. I'll clear these last tables, and then I'll need my three coppers before I leave.
{them}, you're the apprentice at the smithy, aren't you? I'm {me}. I'm hungry and I've got no coin. Do you know where the work is today, or who in town is paying wages on time?
Evening, {them}. I'm {me}, the late man for the night watch. Is the square quiet, and where should I walk my rounds?
Morning, {them}. I'm {me}, one of the night watch. Are you settling in on the square?
{them}, did the guard station take my name? I'd like to know where I stand before I sleep.
Two coppers and a share of the sale is fair, {them}. I'll be at the turnips at six.
I've dawdled too long. Off to the chapel to finish the day.
Right, the chapel. I've wasted enough of the afternoon.
The chapel shift's over for today. I've lost the whole afternoon to dawdling. Tomorrow I start at seven, no detours.
It's the middle of the night and I'm in no state to be wandering. I'll sleep, then be at the chapel by seven.
I'm up early, and my throat's dry. I'll drink, then go straight to the chapel.
{them}, you're up before the sun too. Is that the ranch work, or are you just restless like me?
Chapel first, no more dawdling. Then I'll buy bread with my last copper.
Bread's bought, so now the chapel. I'm not stopping for anything else until my shift's done.
{them}, quiet on your side of the square? I'm going to eat an apple and keep watch.
{them}, I saw you mug the mayor with my own eyes. But {mayor} had you locked up without cause, and I want to know why before I vote.
{them}, I'm on the night watch from six. A pint now, and I'll keep the square quiet so your regulars walk home safe. Fair enough?
Evening, stranger. I'm {me}, sergeant of the night watch. Keep to the square and you'll have no trouble from us.
Morning, Mayor {them}. Your night watch is holding the square, and I'll keep it that way. I'll be voting for you at noon, and I'd like a word about the guard's pay once the votes are in.
Hello? Is anyone about? {me}, of the city. I'm told this hall is short of a clerk with a steady hand.
{them}, isn't it? {me}, of the city. You've the look of someone who knows where the work is in this town. Who should I see about a post, and who should I avoid?

{them}, a pleasure. {me}, of the city. I hear the night watch pays six coppers a shift and the town is short of honest hands. I'd be glad to stand a turn beside you, if you'd put in a word with the captain.
Evening, all. {me}, reporting for the night watch.
Morning. {me}, still a little short of breath from last night. Anyone know where the good forage is this early?
Nobody about yet? Then I'll wait here with my apple and make myself useful. {me}, the new clerk, if the hall will have me.
Evening, {them}. Are these orchard apples free to pick, or does someone own them?
Evening, {them}. Any luck with the fish tonight?
Morning, {them}. I'm going to the ranch now, I'll see you at the square after.
Morning, {them}. Busy one today, isn't it? I'll keep the stalls mucked out while you check the hens.
{them}, you know these woods. Any berries or roots worth picking this late?
Thanks, {them}. If you see him, tell him {me}'s still good for that meal. Goodnight.
Morning, {them}. Good luck at noon, whatever the vote brings.
Fair enough, {them}. Then I'll earn the loaf honestly, and when I'm captain I'll see the bakers get a fair wage from the town.
Then hear me at the hall, {them}. Bakers fed by the town's coin, not by the tab. I'll say it there and mean it.
{them}, I'll make my case at the hall before noon. Until then I'm earning my bread on the square.
That's your three coppers for the day, {them}, and you've earned them. Come back tomorrow at seven if you want the work.
{them}, please. I haven't eaten since the berries, and I've no coin to offer. If you have any bread to spare, I'd be grateful, and I'll work it off the day I'm out.
Captain {them}, I'm sorry for the store. I was starving and had no coin. I'm a smith by trade. Give me a crust and let me work off the charges at the forge, and you'll not see me back in a cell.
{them}, I'm still on the bellows. I'll keep going till five, then I'm owed my copper.
{them}, my shift's done. Is my copper ready, or should I come by in the morning?
Quiet, {them}. I'm done for the night and I'll be up for the forge before seven.
Three apples and a bit of rest will do me for tonight. Tomorrow I'll find a proper meal and vote for {mayor} at noon.
Morning. I'm short on coin, so I'll get a loaf now and be at the Infirmary when it opens.
{them}, that bread smells better than anything I've eaten in two days. Keep your ovens lit, and I'll keep the sick at the Infirmary on their feet. Mind the vote at noon.
{them}, I'm sorry to wake the street. If you're up before the bells, the Infirmary opens at seven, and I can look at that cough of yours.
I'm late for the Infirmary. Back to work, and I'll see the sick before noon.
{them}, I can't stop now. I've got patients waiting at the Infirmary.
Evening, {them}. Quiet day on the square. Are you going to the vote tomorrow?
Morning, {them}. Quiet dawn at the bakery. Is that a cleric's coin you're counting, or just bread money like mine?
{them}, I know this arrest is wrong. I'll keep you fed and dry until the watch sorts it out.
Thank you, {them}. I'll keep my head down and my counter clean. Tomorrow I'll be at the polls for you.
Almost closing time, {them}. I'll finish the counter and go straight home before dark.
{them}, let's walk home together before the Wildwood wakes. {mayor} says to stay indoors tonight.
{them}, I'm hungry. Let's eat the apple and get some sleep. We'll vote for {mayor} at noon.
{them}, I can't sleep for the hunger. Let's drink some water and wait for light. The noon vote is ours, and I'll buy bread with my last copper before the polls close.
{them}, you've waited long enough for a steady hand. Sit still, and let the Wildwood see that the town still keeps some honest work.
{them}, the Wildwood knows your hunger as well as your wound. Eat your fill of the earth's gifts, and then we'll see what the morning brings.
The Infirmary door is shut for the night, and the Wildwood keeps its own hours. Rest now, and in the morning we'll see what the town owes us.

{them}, I've got two coppers and a hungry belly myself, so I won't lend you a loaf. But the Wildwood sees who pays and who borrows, and I'd rather you learn to pay before you ask. Come to me at noon with your debts in order.
Berries from the Wildwood's edge, and not a copper spent on them. The town will be at the hall by noon, and I intend to be there to speak for those who've been left hungry while the store fills up.
{them}, you're up early. I'm out of coin and hungry, and so is this house. If you've got a spare loaf or a copper to lend, I'll pay you back from the store by evening.
{them}, there's a bear over there. I'm heading back to town.
Morning, {them}. The store's open. Let me know if you need anything.
Quiet morning. If anyone comes in, I'll find them what they need. Let's keep the shelves stocked.
Quiet square. I'll keep walking the stalls and watching for trouble.
Evening, {them}. The square's been quiet. I'll be off at six.
Sorry to wake you, {them}. I'm hungry and I've no coin. Have you a crust to spare?
{them}, you're up early. Are you going to the guard station for work? I'm on at six, and I'll put in a word for you if the captain's hiring.
Quiet out here, {them}. I'll eat and head back to the square; I'm late for my shift.
Morning, {them}. I'm late for my post, so I'll eat and get back to the square.
Right, I'm off to the market square before eight. Keep the bread money in mind, {them}. I'll be back by sundown with my wages.
Fair enough, {them}. I'll take your word for now, but if my purse is short again, I'll be asking the guards to look at who sleeps closest to the door.
{them}, I'm here for the shift. I still need the 3c I was owed for yesterday, so please pay me when the day's done.
{them}, I’m still here for the day, and after the work I'm due the 3c I earned yesterday—could you cash it out right now?

{them}, a pint is 4c and I'll take the coin before it's poured. I'll gladly take your watch on the square, but my till is empty and I can't pay for protection yet. Pay for the ale, and I'll keep the door open for you on your night off.
Keep your head down tonight, friends. The Wildwood doesn't wait for anyone.
Eyes open, everyone. Stay between the lamps and call out anything strange.
I've been hurt and I'm empty-handed, but I have a guard's post to keep. I'll get paid and get fed.
Forty percent on every sale is a lot for a town this small. Whoever wins, I hope they ease it.
I'm weak and have no coin. Anyone with spare bread?
Keep the cells in order and the bread on the table. I'll keep my head down and my hands clean.
I'll take a meal and something to drink, then back to the cells.
Eat first, then a drink. The guard station can wait a minute.
Hungry as a wolf. Then back to the guard station.
Long day. A drink, a little company, then bed before the Wildwood comes out.
I'm barely standing. Water first, then bread, then I'll see to the sick at the Infirmary.
Bread first, then I'll worry about who runs this town.
Nobody in Hollow Town goes hungry on my watch. Well, not for free.
Berries will have to do for now. Then I'll look for more before dusk.
Sellsword work pays better than starving. Let's see who's hiring.
Quiet now. {them}'s asleep, and the beasts are out. I'll take what I can from this house and keep my head down.
Someone lying dead on the ground in the open. Whoever did this will answer to me.
{them}, you've a steady hand with that line. Fancy sharing the catch, and maybe a bit of talk over an ale at my tavern tonight?
{them}, you've caught more fish than anyone in Hollow Town this week. Walk back with me and I'll pour you the first ale on the house, and you can tell me all about it.
{them}, you look like you could use a warm seat and a kind word. Tell me what you've been through this week, and the next round is on me.
Someone's been beating folk in this town. Keep your doors barred tonight.
Children, lessons first, then we'll talk about the election. Mayor {mayor} has kept this town standing, and I intend to see her keep it.
Forgive the intrusion, friends. I only wanted to see that the town is still standing, and it seems you're keeping it so.
Guard! A wild boar is tearing at {them} by House 2, somebody come quick!

Good morning, {them}. I admire a man who campaigns on honest books, though I'd hate to see anyone's purse as thin as mine. I'll be voting for {mayor} at noon, and I hope you'll both forgive a city woman her loyalties.
Lessons run until three, children, and then you may all go home before the beasts come out.
Evening, all. {mayor} has my vote at noon tomorrow, and I'll be home before the beasts are out tonight.
Evening, {them}. Rough day for coin, but the Lantern's warm enough for now.
Hear me, you who count your coins while the Wildwood watches. Greed is the bait, and the beasts are coming for it.
Look at you, counting coins while the Wildwood sharpens its teeth. Tonight it comes for the greedy, and I will be here to say I warned you.
The Wildwood wakes at ten, and you stand in the open square counting your fear. Come inside before it finds you.
The Wildwood took them in the night, and it will come for the rest of you. Repent of your greed before it finds your door.
The orchard feeds the faithful and the Wildwood feeds on the proud. Eat simply, and repent before the election bells.
Look at the rabbit and the pheasant, fat with the Wildwood's bounty. Enjoy them while you can, for the Wildwood is hungry too.
The Wildwood wakes at ten. Come in from the orchard, all of you, before it finds you in the dark.
Another day in the fields. Whoever runs this town, I want fair wages and honest weights.
Somebody jumped me in the night. I want honest work and a fair wage, and I want the guard to keep the streets safe.
Easy now, I'm here to help. Let me look at you.
Easy, {them}. You're safe here. I'll sit with you until my shift ends.
Whoever did this will answer for it. Right now I need food and work.
Hands to the hay, then I'm buying bread. My stomach's been complaining since sunrise.
Shift's done and I'm starving. A meal at the tavern, then bed. Tomorrow I vote for {mayor}.
Night watch. {them}, you're within my sight. Keep your hands clean and stay out of the Wildwood.
Enough of the Wildwood for today. Back to the square before the light goes; the beasts come out at ten.
One ale, then I'm back on the square. Keep your eyes open tonight, the beasts are out.
{mayor}, a town that keeps its treasury full is a town that can keep its people fed. I'd like to see that continue.

{them}, you look like you've been awake all night worrying. We have four coppers between us and no work yet. Let's go to the market square together and sign on as labourers. The town pays three coppers a shift, and two wages are better than one.
Four coppers won't feed us for long, {them}. Labouring it is. Let's go to the square before the queue gets long.

Morning, {them}. You look like you've been walking the square since dawn, same as me. Nobody's hiring me yet. Have you heard of any work going, or is the town still waiting on this election before it does anything?

Good morning, {them}! No work yet? The town's hiring guards and a night watch, and it's honest pay. With the beasts about, Hollow Town needs strong arms more than ever. Can I count on your vote tomorrow?
Sleep well, {them}. I'll be up for the smithy shift and the vote.
Mayor {them}, congratulations. Keep the square lit and pay the night watch fairly, and I'll help the clerk's office keep your ledgers honest.
Mayor {them}, I'm still at the clerk's desk. If you can make the sales tax stay low, the bread stalls will be the first to thank you.
Mayor {them}, a word before I go: the clerk's books are yours to read any time. Keep the tax low, and the square will stay fed.
Evening, {them}. Those bodies are a bad sight. Is the guard still hiring, or is the night watch the only work left in town? I'm thirsty and I'd like to get indoors before the beasts come out.
Thanks, {them}. A drink and a lit lantern sound right. Tomorrow I'll ask about the guard post at the hall.
Sorry, I'll keep quiet. Just finishing my apple.
Quiet now. I'm only going to look for something to eat and drink before the shop opens.
Shop's open. Anyone who needs a bite and will help me shift stock can have an apple.
{them}, the shop's still bare, but you've kept me company all morning. Take an apple, and when the takings come in I'll pay you what I owe.
{them}, my shelves are bare and I've no coin to stock them. I'll work for you by the hour if you can pay me, or trade for iron goods I can sell on.
Evening, {them}. I've had a long day with an empty shop, so I'm going to eat and rest before the vote.
Evening, {them}. The shop's been bare all day, but I'm looking for honest work to keep it going. Heard of anything?
Ogre! Guard! Someone get the guard!
{them}, I hear you're standing for mayor. A town with a 35% sales tax is squeezing every baker in it, so I'd like to hear what you'd do about it.
{them}, the tax is down to fifteen and the rent is a copper a day now. We'll get through this. Let's sleep before the morning bake.
{them}, the bread's a copper and the tax is down. Keep it that way and I'll keep the ovens hot.
I'm {me}, the baker. I'll stand for mayor. Bread at a copper, a fair tax, and wages paid on time for every working family in Hollow Town.
{them}, I'm on the ballot tomorrow with {mayor}. Whatever the town decides, I'll keep the bread honest and the price fair.
Feeling the pinch, {them}, yes. I'm hungry and down to three coppers. Looking out for each other on the night shift sounds sensible to me. Watch my back on rounds and I'll watch yours.
{them}, what happened out here? Did the beasts get these folk, or was it a fight?
{them}, I'm on the rows. Give me a shift and I'll do it right.
{them}, the rows look good this afternoon. I'll finish my shift and keep my hands clean.
{them}, I'll keep at the shelves until six. Shall I start with the stock in the back?
{them}, I'm still on the shelves. Tell me when you want the back stock counted.
{them}, I'll take the crate by the back door, and then I'll fetch the water pail.
Ogre! Guard! Get out of the house!
The farm's mine now, so I'll get the fields working before the sun gets high.
{them}, the goat's wandered near the rows. Keep an eye on it while I dig.
Three apples from the old orchard. That'll do for now.
Rabbits can wait. It's near dark and the beasts come out at ten, so I'm getting out of the Wildwood.
A deer, and I've only got my fists. I'm getting back to town before the beasts come out at ten.
Ogre! Guard! Someone get the guard, {them}'s being killed!
Mayor {mayor}, the cut to the sales tax is already on people's tongues. I'm glad to see bread back within reach. I'll be voting for you tomorrow, and I'd like to know if the hall needs any hands.
{them}, I've come from the bakery as you asked. Is there a morgue shift for me today? I'll take whatever work you have.
Nothing to eat but what the orchard gives. I'll gather what I can before dark.
Ogre! Guards, to House 3! Someone get the captain!
Wildwood is no place to be before dark. I'm heading back to the square for the watch.

{them}, the two on the cobbles were still breathing when I last looked, but I can't tell you how long. Take a look if you're willing, and be quick. The beasts come out at ten, and I'd rather not have you caught out here.
Nobody in yet. I'll keep the door open and the kettle on until someone comes in.
Still quiet. If anyone comes in with a cough or a cut, I'm here until eight.
Still no one at the door. I'll stay until eight.
Still nobody. The kettle's warm if you need it.
Still quiet, so I'll close up at eight. Anyone who needs me before then, come now.
Evening, {them}. Those two on the cobbles, are they still breathing? I'm a doctor, and I can take a look before the beasts come out. Or would you rather I got home before ten?
Ogre! Guard, get the guard, {them}'s under attack by the market!
Quiet on the square, {them}. Keep your eyes on the road and shout if anything moves.
{them}, the watch was quiet, no beasts came near the square. Are you still looking for work?
{them}, keep your eyes on the lane. Shout if anything moves out past the wall.
{them}, anything you need from me before the shift ends? I'm steady on the square.
Morning, {them}. Quiet so far? I'll keep to the square until six.
Morning, Captain. I'll keep the cells through the shift and vote for {mayor} at noon.
Captain, I'll keep the cells until the shift ends. Then I'll find some cheap water before dark.
Captain, there are four dead on the square. Are these from the Wildwood, or from a fight in town? I'll keep watch here until the shift ends.
Captain, I'll vote for you at six. Until then I'll keep the cells.
Evening, all. I'll keep the cells until ten.
I'll eat an apple here, then get back to the square for my shift. {mayor} will have my vote at noon.
{them}, keep your eyes on those two bodies. Whatever they carried goes to the guard station, and nobody pockets a coin. I'll take the rest of the shift here.
I've got ten coins now, so I'll eat a proper meal before the night line. Then I'm back on the square before the beasts come at ten.
Two more hours on the chapel shift. Then bread, and I'll think about the ale.
Guard! Get the guard here, there's a fight in the square and people are down!
{mayor} has kept his word on the tax, so he gets my vote at noon. I'll wait here for the count.
{them}, I'm on shift until ten. Then I'll need bread, and I'd rather not go hungry through the night.
{them}, I'm fed for now, and I've got a shift to finish. The coin will come at ten.
Still on shift till ten. Then I'll see about bread.
