Could anyone spare a copper for a hungry man? I've got one coin and nothing else.
It's too late for the bakery. I'll take my three coppers out of savings, and then I need sleep before the beasts are out.
The bakery should be open. I'll buy bread with my own three coppers, not the treasury, then I'll be at the hall for the vote.
Bread first, then I'll see to the rest. The vote is at noon and I'll stand by my platform.
{them}, I'm still on the ballot and still mayor, so I'll keep to the books. Let's see what work there is at the hall.
{them}, I have one copper and a mayor's wage coming. Let's see what work there is before the vote tomorrow.
The beasts come at ten and I have one copper. I'll spend the evening at the tavern, keep off the streets, and sleep before the dark.
Ogre! Guards, to House 5, now!
Two coins for my vote, Mayor? Done. You've got my vote tomorrow, and I'll keep my ears open for work.
Keep the square quiet, and keep your coin close. {mayor}'s treasury is the one thing this town can count on.
That's the shift done. Nobody out past dark once the beasts come out of the Wildwood.
Quiet night. I'll sleep before the beasts are out and face the vote with a clear head.
Deal, {them}. You watch my back on rounds and I'll watch yours. We'll both be better off than starving alone.
{them}, I'm on the mayor's ballot now, against {mayor}. I'd rather see the sales tax cut so people can afford bread. Keep an ear out for me.
Help! Someone's attacked me, I'm barely standing. Guards, to me!
{them}, I'll hear you out after I close up. Let me finish this shift first.
{them}, you've kept the square lit and cut the tax to 15%. Bread's easier to afford now. I'm voting for you at noon. Is the Market square guard or the Drowned Lantern still hiring?
{them}, are you working here at the Infirmary? I'm a server at the Drowned Lantern, and I'm always glad to hear of honest work or a good cure.
{them}, I hear you run the Lantern now. I'm here for my server shift from four. Are the tips and the ale wages still the same under you?
{them}, I'm sorry to see the morgue so busy. If you know of any honest work, I'd be glad to hear it. I'm off to my server shift at four.
{them}, sleep. I'll be back once the Lantern closes, and I'll bring food if the tips are kind.
{them} has had her turn at the treasury. Hollow Town needs someone who knows what the working folk pay in taxes. Vote {me}, and the sales tax comes down.
Bread and ale for the room, and I'll stand you a round. Tomorrow the town votes, and I want every one of you to remember who kept your belly full tonight.

{them}, you're on the night guard. I'm {me}, and I run the Drowned Lantern. I need a sharp pair of eyes on the town after dark, and I'm standing for mayor at noon. A guard who helps me win keeps a good job.
Keep your head down out there too, {them}. Good night.
{them}, you've got the look of someone who's been on her feet since dawn. Sit a moment, and tell me how the bakery treated you.
{them}, sit by the stove a minute. Whatever the bakery paid you, we'll make it stretch. Then tell me what you noticed about the town today.
{them}, you look as done in as I am. Have a berry, and we'll finish the cart before the bells.
{them}, one more crate for the cart and then we can wash up. I'm thirsty enough to drink the chapel well dry.
{them}, good work today. Lock up the chapel, and I'll buy you a drink on the next wage I'm promised by a gentleman of the city.
Hear me, you who hoard coin while the bread goes stale. The Wildwood watches this town, and it counts every coin you keep.
Honest work, {them}? I'll take any work that keeps my hands clean and my purse full. Tell me what you need done, and I'll see it done. Mark my words, the Wildwood is watching this town.
Eat your bread while you can, neighbours. The Wildwood counts the hours until ten, and it will not care whose purse was full.
Water, friend, if the cellar has any. I've no wish to be found on the road after dark, and the Wildwood has no mercy for the unwary.
{them}, let's finish this shift properly. Work done honestly is the only kind I'll put my name to.
{them}, keep at it. Honest coin, honest work.
{them}, let's get this iron finished. Honest work, honest pay.
{them}, one more stretch on the anvil, then we'll see what the day has paid us.
{them}, you keep a busy house. If you need a steady hand, I'd rather work for honest coin than sit idle.
{them}, nobody's hiring anyone decent until the mayor's race settles. Keep your ears open at the Lantern tonight. Good luck finding something.
Hard morning out here, {them}. Ground's softer than it looks. Let's keep at it.
Long day in the fields. Goodnight, {them}.
Can't sleep with my stomach growling. Morning, {them}.

Morning, {them}. Neither of us has work, and the beasts come out of the Wildwood at ten tonight, so we shouldn't be out in the open after dark. The labourer's job at the market square starts at eight and pays 3c a shift. Want to walk over together and see if they'll take us both?
Good. Then let's get there before the line forms. Keep up, {them}.

{them}, we have nothing in our purse and the sun's barely up. The labourers hire at the market square from eight for three coins a day. Stop staring at the ground and come with me before the line gets long.
Morning. You look like you're looking for work too. What are you good at?

I don't know who's hiring yet, but the town pays labourers 3c at the market square from eight. Let's go ask at the hall before the work's gone. And tell me more about this Wildwood business, because nobody's told me anything useful yet.
Beasts at night, then. Fine, I'll believe it when I see the marks. Let's go to the hall.
Right, {them}. Three coppers is three coppers, and you're right, I've been staring at the ground long enough. Lead on, and let's get in line before it grows.
Morning, {them}. You're out of work too? The town pays labourers at the market square from eight, three coppers a shift. Let's go together and see if they'll take us both.
Aye, I'm out of work too, {them}. Three coppers a shift beats sitting on my hands. Let's walk over to the market square together and see if they'll take us both.
Three coppers a shift, and the market square from eight. Lead the way, {them}. I'd rather be paid than watch the beasts come out tonight with nothing in my pocket.
Work, yes, though I came for more than wages. Mark me, {them}: the Wildwood hears this town's greed, and it will come for the greedy. Stay near people who will pray with you.

Labourer's wage at the square, good. Come, let's get to the hall before the line forms. As for the Wildwood: it's no tale. Every night at ten the beasts come out of it and take whoever is caught in the open. The greedy ones who lock their doors and count their coins are the first to be found. I've seen the signs, and I've felt it in my bones since I was a boy.

Honest coin? Labourers are wanted at the market square from eight, three coppers a shift. It's not much, but it's a start, and a girl who works hard gets noticed. Want to walk over together? I know a lot of people in this town, and I'd like to know more.
Lead the way, {them}. Three coppers each, and we both get noticed by the whole square. Let's go before the crowd gets there first.
There's a guard's badge with your name on it, {them}. That's 4c a day from the town. Stand with me at noon tomorrow and it's yours.
Done, {them}. If the bakery ever lets you down, the badge is yours. Now get indoors before ten.
Mourn tonight, friends. Tomorrow we hold together.
Doors barred by ten, neighbours. The guard is out there for you.
Rest easy, Hollow Town. The guard keeps watch.
Bar your doors, Hollow Town. The guard has the night.
{them}, I picked up a short sword for protection. The roads and the Wildwood aren't safe, and I'd rather not be caught empty-handed.
{them}, I'm hungry and the tax is eating us alive. Tomorrow I'm back on the fields, and then I'm going to the hall to stand for mayor myself.
{them}, I'm at the edge of the Wildwood with a sword. If the boar comes out, I'd rather be on this side of it. Let's see what the day brings.
{them}, I'm on the fields until the bell. We'll need every hand we can get before this tax takes the last of us.
{them}, the mayor's seat is empty and the tax is at 140%. Whoever stands tomorrow had better promise to cut it.
{them}, good to meet you. I'm {me}. I'm in the same boat as you, looking for steady work. I'll keep my ears open, and if I hear of an opening I'll tell you straight away.
Guard! A bear is attacking {them} right here at House 3! Somebody bring a light and help!
{them}, the farm's hungry for hands. I'll work the fields for you once it's light, if you've got a shift.
Quiet on the square. Keep your purses close, all of you, and report anything odd before dark.
Quiet night. Stay inside, {them}, and keep the door barred till light.
{them}, I'm {me}. I've got a farmhand's hands and no pay yet. Is there a shift I can take on, even for a few hours?
{them}, I'm {me}. I missed the afternoon shift at the fields and I'm short on rent. Do you have any work at the tavern, even washing cups?
Time to get out of the Wildwood before the beasts come.
{them}, hold on. I'm going for the guard.
I'm starving and out of coin. I'll get some bread before the bakery shuts.
Nothing open at this hour, and I've got two coppers. I'll drink and wait for the bakery to open.
I'll eat this fish, then get back to town before the vote.
{them}, I'm between shifts and short of coin. Do you have any work for a clerk, or a copper to spare?
One fish, a quiet night indoors, and then I'll see what work is going at the schoolhouse tomorrow.
I've got no coin for ale, and the Wildwood beasts will be out soon. I'm going home to sleep.
I'm thirsty and broke, and the sales tax is now 140%. I'll wait here until morning and then look for work and food.
Work first, then I'll eat my berries and head home before dark.
The schoolhouse bell's still ringing, so I'll go teach what I can before the day ends. I'll keep my two berries for later.
{them}, any word on the river fish tomorrow? I've got no coin, but I can share news from the schoolhouse.
Guard! An ogre's in House 4, it's tearing into {them}! Somebody get the captain!
I've got three apples, so I'll eat one now and save the rest. Then I'll get back to the ranch before my shift is missed.
Ranch has a new boss, {them}. I'll keep my head down, get a drink, and see if she still needs hands.
Quiet now, {them}. I'll eat my last apple and get some rest before the morning shift.
{them}, the sales tax is at 140% and nobody can afford bread. I'm going to the ranch for my shift, and at noon I'm voting against {mayor}.
Nobody about, so I'll get on with the rows until the shift ends.
Long shift done. I'll get some rest by the chapel stove and keep the apple for tomorrow.
Thirsty and hungry, but I'll make do with the apple and sleep by the stove. Fields at six.
Quiet, {them}. I'm off to forage before the fields. Hunger's worse than the cold.
Berries will do for now. Then I'll get myself back to the fields before I lose the day's wage.
{them}, the shift's done. Any word on where a man can get a bed cheaper than the chapel stove?
Goodnight, {them}. I'll go to the chapel stove. The beasts come out at ten, so I'm not lingering here.
{them}, I'm sorry to ask, but I've had nothing since the berries. Could you spare a bite or a copper? I'll pay you back when the ranch turns a profit.
{them}, thank you for listening to me last night. I'm going to the ranch now to start the feeding. I'll be back with food for us both.
{them}, I've got two coppers and an empty stomach, so I'll keep working the ranch and fish the stream for our supper. Let's get these hens fed first.
{them}, I'm {me}, the rancher up at Thorncroft. Mind if I fish beside you? I'll share what I catch.
Two fish for supper, and then I need a bed. Tomorrow I'll get the ranch running properly.
Guard! There's an ogre on {them} at House 6, get help here!
{them}, you look like you've been up all night too. Anything worth knowing about who's hiring, or who's been light-fingered around here?
Somebody's been beating on me in the dark. I want the guard on this, now.
{them}, I need hands on the Lantern floor and I pay fair. Take a shift tonight, and we'll talk about the rest of the town after.
{them}, the Lantern is open until midnight. Ale's four coppers, and I'll pay a fair wage to anyone who keeps the floor honest tomorrow.
{them}, the sun's barely up and the square's already hungry. Walk with me to the fields, and I'll show you how a man keeps himself fed without asking the town for charity.
{them}, the shift's done. Is there word on the election, or any work on your farm?
Goodnight, {them}. Quiet tonight, please.
Quiet night. I'll eat from my pack and wait for daylight.
{them}, I'm home. There's no mayor now, so we'll need to see who stands at the hall tomorrow.
Afternoon, {them}. Let me see to your hurts, then I'll get something in my belly.
{them}, hold still while I look at that. Then I'll see what this fish fetches.
Shift ends at eight, but the Infirmary stays open for anyone who comes through the door tonight.
Five coppers, and the tax has eaten most of what the fish was worth. I'll wet my throat and get some sleep before the vote.
Five coppers won't buy much with the tax at 140%. I'll see what the hedgerows give before first light.
I'm starving, and five coppers still have to last. Bread first, then the vote.
Quiet afternoon. I'll keep the Infirmary open, and I'll ask about my wage at the end of the shift.
{them}, the bear came into House 7 last night and nearly took my wife. {mayor} has promised a bounty on the beasts. I'm voting for him at noon, and I'd like to hear your view before then.
{them}, a meal for me, and I'll take it on credit against my next shift if you have work for a sellsword.
{them}, I'm a sellsword with fists and a strong back. Is there any paid job in this town today?
{them}, I'm heading to the market square to take my post. Stay close to the lanterns tonight.
{them}, I'm still on the night watch. Keep your eyes on the square and shout if anything comes out of the Wildwood.
I've got four coppers and an empty belly. I'll get bread and a turnip before I take my shift.
{them}, I'm back on the market square for the night watch. Keep an eye out for anything coming from the Wildwood.
Quiet night so far. I'll keep my post on the market square until dawn and watch for anything from the Wildwood.
{them}, is that someone lying there? I'll check on him before I take my post.
Still at the chapel. I'll eat this apple and keep at the undertaking.
Shift's nearly done. I'll collect my wage and find something to eat.
It's the dead of night, I'm not walking the streets. I'll rest here and eat in the morning.
{them}, is there more to do here? I'll keep at the undertaking until my shift ends.
Still at the chapel, {them}. Hungry, but the shift pays and I'll stick to it.
Shift's nearly over, {them}. I'll collect my wage, then get something hot at the Lantern before dark.
{them}! There you are. Let's talk about that partnership over a drink, then I'll find a bed.
{them}, I'm {me}. I'm short on coin and I'll work a shift for you. Whatever needs doing, I'll do it.
{mayor} gets my vote at noon, and I'll look for honest work before then.
{them}, I'm {me}. I'm short on coin and I'll work honest for anyone who's hiring.
{them}, I've got no coin left and I'm hungry. Give me any shift you've got and I'll earn my meal.
{them}, the ovens are cooling and my shift's done. Any word on who's hiring once {mayor} wins?
{mayor}, I'll stand with you at noon. A guard's badge and a steady wage is more than I had this morning. You have my vote.
{them}, I'm starving. I'm going to the tavern for a meal before the captain vote.
{them}, I'm back on the square. Let's keep the peace and get through the shift.

Three coppers is more than I've got, {them}. I'm after anything that pays. Work, a loose purse, a way to eat through the week. If you know where coin is going spare, or who's hiring, I'll listen. And I'll share what I know in return.
{them}, I've got no coin for ale, so I'll find food and water myself. Labourer's pay in the square tomorrow is the plan.
Bear! Guard, there's a bear on {them}! Get inside, everyone!
{them}, I'm on the counter until six. If you need anything weighed or wrapped, I'm your clerk.
{them}, I'm not staying out here with that body and the beasts about. I'm going to the square, where the guards are, and I'll see you at noon.
{them}, I'm leaving this house now. The beasts come at night, and I want to be on the square with the guards before anything else happens.
I'll eat an apple here, then get back to the square before noon to vote.
{them}, I'm back on the counter. Anything you need weighed or wrapped, just ask.
{them}, I've got no coin left, but I'm honest and I work hard. If you need a server for the late shift, I'll take it for 3c.
Hear me, all of you. Every coin you hoard from your neighbour is a nail in the Wildwood's door. Keep your doors barred after dark, and come to me before the Wildwood comes to you.

{them}, a doctor. Good. When the Wildwood's beasts come at 22:00, I'll be counting the dead, and I'd rather not count you. Will you keep your infirmary open for the living, or only for those who can pay?
Good. Then keep that promise, {them}. I'll be at the morgue all day, and I'd rather bring you the living than the dead.
Agreed, {them}. The living first. Now go on, I've work waiting.
{them}, I have no coin for bread and no ale for my thirst. Can you spare a turnip, or should I go hungry into the Wildwood's night?

{them}, I hear you're standing for mayor too. A town with a 70% sales tax needs a candidate who understands what a shopkeeper and a server both have to pay. I'd like to hear your platform before noon.
Forgive me, I'm only passing through. I've had nothing since yesterday, and I'd be grateful for any scrap you can spare.
{them}, is the ranch hiring? I'd rather work an honest shift than go hungry another day.
{them}, I'll take the tables by the hearth. Keep the trays coming and I'll keep the ale moving.
Morning. I'm {me}. Looks like you're hunting for work too. What are you good at, {them}?
Labourer's work at the market square starts at eight. Let's go see if they're taking on hands, {them}.
Morning, {them}. I'm {me}. I hear the town is hiring labourers, and I'm ready to work.
Quiet shop today. I'll stay open and see who comes in.
Honest work sounds good to me, {them}. I'm not proud. What's going on at the bakery or the shops, is anyone hiring?
Thanks, {them}. I'll head to the bakery now and see if the owner will take me on.
The bakery's hiring a hand, I think. Baker's hand, 4 to 13, three coppers a shift from the owner. The shops are a bit thin. Head down there before the morning's out, {them}.
Good luck, {them}. Tell the baker I sent you.
{them}, I heard you. We've got nothing, so we work for it. Let's find honest work first and build from there.

{them}, my friend, you look like a man who has never once been asked what he's truly worth. Tell me about yourself. I have a feeling we could be useful to each other, and I'm a man of some standing in the city, so be assured the rewards will be generous.
Morning, {them}. Looking for work? The town pays guards and labourers, and I can find you a place. All I ask is your vote at noon tomorrow.
Then lease a shop at the hall and hand out wages of your own, {them}. My vote stays with me. The offer stands if you change your mind.
Five coppers and a guard post if you want it, {them}. That's my last word. Run if you like, but the guards answer to me.
Keep together tonight, friends. Beasts come at ten.
Morning, {them}. {me}. I'm looking for steady work, and I'd like to hear what's going on in this town.
{them}, I'm going to find something to eat before I sleep. Tomorrow I'll vote for {mayor} at noon. You should too, if you want the guard paid.
Morning, {them}. I've no coin yet, but I've got two good hands and sharp eyes. Know of anyone who needs them?
Thank you, {them}. I can work a field, mind a till, and I have sharp eyes and a steady head. Where's the right door? I'll take whatever honest work pays.
Morning, {them}. Looking for work? I'm in the same boat, no coin and a wife to feed. Anything going at all?
{them}, keep me in mind. If anything turns up, I'll take it, and I'll do the same for you.
{them}, I've had a long day with no coin. Let's eat the apples and rest. Tomorrow I'll find work.
{them}, you're up early too. I'm {me}, the clerk at the hall. Quiet out here, isn't it?
Same boat as you, {them}. Nobody's coin is spare this morning, but I'll ask around. Let's see who's hiring before the day's gone.
{them}, fifty percent on the sales tax and five copper a day in rent? I've got nothing to pay either with. Is the town going to let a man like me eat this winter?
{them}, keep an eye on the tables for me a minute. I've got a shift to finish and a thirst to see to.
Morning, {them}. Do you know who's hiring today? I've got nothing in my purse and I'm not proud about it.
Morning. I'm new in town with one coin to my name, and I'm looking for honest work. Know of anyone hiring?
Afternoon, {them}. I hear you're running for mayor. I'm going with {mayor}, but I'll hear you out over a drink.

{them}, you look like a man who's been looking for work all morning. Tell me, what can you do with your hands? I've got four coppers and a sharp tongue, and I'm thinking of standing for mayor. Could use someone who knows the town.
{them}, fifty percent sales tax and five coppers a day in rent will bleed this town dry. I'm looking for honest work, and I'll be watching how you answer that at the polls.
{them}, I'm too tired to be useful tonight. We'll talk in the morning.
Marta, I hear you about the Wildwood. I'll think on it after I've had some bread.
Marta, you've got a point about the Wildwood. I'll stand for mayor myself. Folk are paying too much in tax and rent, and I'll cut both.
Folk of Thornfield, I'm on the ballot. Cut the half-tax on your bread and the rent on your roof, and keep the guard honest.
Evening, folk. I'm {me}, cleric at the chapel and on the ballot tomorrow. Half the bread price goes to the hall, and I want that stopped.
{them}, I'm running the general store now. Come by if you need supplies, and I'll keep my prices fair.
{them}, the store's open till six. Bread's a copper and eggs are a copper, if you've got one to spare.
{them}, I'll trade you a good word for the orchard's windfalls, if you've got any spare.
Someone's in trouble here! I'm going for the guard.
Good morning, friends. I'm {me}, a guard who means to keep this town honest.
A drink, then back to the square. The night is mine to keep honest.
Hold! Bear, drop him! I'm the night guard, and you're under arrest!
Hands are fine, {them}. I can carry, mind a door, and I know every lane between here and the river. Give me honest pay and I'll work for your campaign.
Morning, {them}. I'm here for the shift. Tell me where you want the stock counted first.
Still at it, {them}. Tell me what needs doing before six.
{them}, I'm sorry to wake you. I've had nothing since yesterday and no coin in my purse. Have you a crust to spare?
Morning, {them}. I've got a shift at the ranch to get to, but I'll keep an ear out for work.
{them}, I'm on the ranch crew. Point me at the next job and I'll see it done.
{them}, I've got two apples and a guard's shift to finish. Let's keep this square quiet today.
Three bodies on this square. Stay back and let me look. Who saw what happened here?
Thanks, {them}. The guard captain's crew it is. And I'll mind who I take a shilling from, you can count on that.
Hungry work for four coppers. A turnip will have to do until my shift's out.
Morning. Undertaker's shift at the chapel. Somebody has to keep the dead in order.
Evening, {them}. Sorry, I'm short on coin and empty in the belly. Is there a shift left on the square?
Evening, {them}. Long day at the chapel. Are you here for the cure or just passing through?
Two faces might be harder to turn away, {them}. Fine by me. But the Lantern hires after dark, and I'd rather not walk in there blind. Let's get to the hall first and see what's on offer in daylight.
{them}, I've got a schoolteaching post to get to by nine. Come find me at the hall after, and we'll see about the Lantern together.
Morning, all. I'm keeping the square honest, and I'll back the mayor's choice for captain.
Evening, {them}. Long shift. Care to share a drink before we turn in?
Morning, {them}. Doctor's shift at the Infirmary won't wait, so I'll see you around.
Busy enough, {them}. Come by if your ribs ever start complaining. I'm heading there now.
{them}, I'm a doctor here, so if you're hurt, sit down and let me look at you.
{them}, the mayor's seat is empty and nobody's on the ballot. I'll have a drink, then see who stands at noon.
{them}, it's the middle of the night and I'm the Infirmary doctor. Did anyone tell you the mayor's race is open at noon?
{them}, you're on the late watch with me. Keep your eyes open on the square tonight, and we'll talk about the vote in the morning.
{them}, keep an eye on the square. Someone's down over there, and I want to see who it is before anyone touches them.
{them}, with me. Three down in the square is more than a brawl. We check whether they're breathing before anyone touches their purses.
{them}, the square's been quiet since the bodies. I'll keep watch here until the vote, and we'll sort out the dead once the captain's word is settled.
Evening. I'm out past the square, so I'll head for the tavern and make my way back before the vote.

{them}, you look like someone who's been waiting on a break. Me too. I've got no work and two coppers to my name. Have you heard anything about the Drowned Lantern hiring, or where the honest coin is in this town?
{them}, if the Lantern's thin, we can find better. Fancy walking with me to see who's hiring?
Sensible. Daylight it is, {them}. We'll see who's hiring at the hall and walk in together.
{them}, I've got the ranch running now. Stay a minute while I see to the animals, then we'll head to the hall together.
The taxes and rent have doubled overnight. Someone needs to say it plainly: a man can't feed himself on those prices.
Apples will do for supper. Then I'll get some rest before the animals need seeing to in the morning.
{them}, good morning! {me}, though most folks call me the one with the sharpest eye for a fine match. You look like someone who knows everybody in this town. Who should I be getting to know first?
{them}, I hear you want hands with a good head and sharp eyes. Put me on the hardest job in this forge and I'll show you what I can do before the shift ends.
Morning, {them}. You look like a man without a shift today. Is there work you're after, or are you just watching the square like the rest of us?
{them}, rent's gone to five a day and the sales tax to half. I can't afford to be a person in this town at those prices, and I'm not the only one.
{mayor}, I'll keep your job offer in mind. This town's money runs through more hands than yours, and I mean to hold a few of them.
Two coppers for my vote? I'm worth more than that, {them}. Make it ten and you'll have it at noon. Or I stand against you and every guard job in this town goes to my friends instead.
Friends, {mayor} wants your vote for five coppers. I want it for a fair town with cheaper rent. Ask yourselves which of us has ever paid you what you're worth.
Drinks are on the house tonight for anyone who'll hear me out. {mayor}'s rent is five coppers a day. Mine will be lower, and the guard will answer to the town, not to his purse.
Bear! {them}, get behind me! Guard, over here, now!
Nothing in the purse yet, but a man who knows the hedgerows never goes hungry for long.
Quiet morning at the forge. Nothing to show for my name yet, but the fire's still warm and the rent has to be met somehow.
Hungry, but the forge is cold and the rent won't pay itself. Let me eat these berries and see who needs a hand.
Guard! A wild boar is on {them} at House 2. Somebody with a spear, get out there before he's gored!
Guard! That boar is goring {them} at House 2! Somebody with a spear, now!
{them}, you're asleep on the step and the guard's about to change. Get yourself up before the captain sees you, and mind the night beat, you'll want your wits about you tonight.
Quiet night on the square. I'll keep my eyes open, and I'll have the coins I left at home by morning.

{them}, good morning. You've the look of a man who's worked the night and hasn't slept. The Wildwood has been watching this town's greed, and it won't wait much longer. Who do you mean to vote for as captain? I'd like a guard in that chair who knows the value of a fair cell and a cold conscience.
Long day, and the farm is paying off. I'll eat well tonight and rest before the vote.
Nothing in the purse, so I'll make do with what the land gives. A goat's no meal for a man, but the fields will feed us once the harvest is in.
{them}, we're both short of coin, so let's work the fields together and see what the harvest brings.
{them}, the loaves will be out within the hour. Keep an eye on the oven for me.
Stay near a guard tonight, friends. The watch is out at ten.
Rest now. The watch holds.
Anyone willing to stand the night watch, come and see me. 4c, paid every day.
Stay together after dark, friends. The beasts hunt the ones who are alone.
Sleep while you can. Tomorrow we get ready for the ogre.
To the square, everyone. Bring what you can swing.
Right behind me, then. Let's see if the foreman's hiring before the rest of this crowd gets to him.
I need a drink, then I'm at the market square for the night watch.
Right behind you, {them}. Lead the way to the foreman.
Right, {them}. Let's get the fields turned before the heat sets in.
A meal and an ale, then home before the Wildwood wakes.
Looks like the ranch is mine to run, so I'll get the animals seen to before the day's out.
Easy, girl. Let's see to the hens and the cow before the heat gets to them.
Steady now. Three cows and two sheep to see to, and the hens want feeding before noon.
Four hens and a sheep left to see to. Then I'll be thinking about where to sleep tonight, with the beasts coming.
Nine animals and I'm the only one minding them. Shift ends at three, then I'm finding a lock and a bed before dark.
Just over an hour left on the shift. Keep the cows calm, lads, and I'll see you fed.
Last sheep and then I'm done. Give me a moment to get some water in me.
Shift's done. I'll get a meal in me, then bar the door before the beasts come out.
{them}, I'm broke and I'll work for my supper. What's needed behind the bar?
{them}, I'm in. I've got nothing but my fists and two berries, so let's see what the captain will pay. Lead the way to the guard station.
{them}, I'm hungry and out of coin. I'll eat my last berry and keep to the house until morning.
{them}, it's still dark and the beasts are out. I'm staying put with the door barred until the sun's up.
{them}, thank you. That apple means more than you know. I'll keep my ears open for work, and I'll tell you first if I hear of anything at the Lantern.
{them}, I'm a sellsword with a sword arm and no coin. I need night watch work before the beasts come out tonight.
{them}, I've been hanging around all day for a shift. Put me to work, even for a plate of stew and a bed by the hearth tonight.
Ogre! Guards, the ogre's on {them} at House 7! Get back to the lamps, I'm not fighting that with my fists!
{them}, good morning. I'm off to the market for the Labourer post. Mind the hall for me.
{them}, I seem to have landed in the schoolhouse with a teacher's post. Let's see whether I can teach you something before the beasts come.
{them}, take a seat. We've got lessons until three, and then the beasts won't be the only thing on your mind.
{them}, you're doing fine. Keep your slate tidy and we'll be done at three.
Quiet schoolhouse this afternoon. I'll keep the lessons going until three, and then I'll see about the rest of the day.
That's the bell for the schoolhouse. I'll wet my throat at the tavern, then find a lit door before the beasts come out.
{them}, I'll eat quick at the Drowned Lantern, then I'm with you at the Wildwood edge before the beasts come out.
Morning. Guard shift on the square. I'll vote for {mayor} at noon.
{them}, we're not beaten yet. Let's pool what we have, find work today, and get a roof and a weapon before the beasts come out at dusk.
{them}, bar the door and keep your eyes open. The beasts come at ten, and anyone who sleeps in a house with a loose latch is asking for trouble. We'll take turns watching till dawn.
Nobody sleep in these houses tonight. The boar hunts by scent. Come to the Drowned Lantern where there are people and a door we can bar.
Nobody is coming to rescue us at this hour, so I'll look for anything edible nearby before the light comes.

Captain {them}, I'm no criminal, just a sellsword with an empty purse and an empty belly. Hire me as a guard, and I'll help you clear the bodies from House 3 and get them to the guard station so their families can claim what they carried.
{them}, I'm {me}. I've got fists and a willingness to work. Is there labouring to be had on these fields?
Nobody sleeps in this house tonight. Eat what you have and come to the Drowned Lantern with me before the boar comes out at ten.
{mayor}, I'm off to the town hall for my clerk shift. I'll be voting for you tomorrow, so don't forget the sales tax.
{them}, I'm at my desk. Tell me what the clerk's work needs doing first.
{them}, how's the clerk's work going? I need my three coppers before the shop prices get any worse.
{them}, I'll stay at my desk until five. Then I'm off for bread, because I haven't eaten since yesterday.
{them}, I'm out of coin, so I'll have to pass on the ale. I'm heading back to the town hall to finish my clerk shift.
{them}, I'm still here at the desk. Once my shift ends at five I'll go for bread and find something to keep the beasts off me.
Nobody's at the desk, so I'll wait here until someone comes back. My shift still pays until five.
{mayor}, I'm staying awake with you tonight. The beasts hunt by scent even in houses, so let's keep the lamp lit and watch the door.
Nobody about, so I'll keep my own counsel. {mayor}'s mayor, I'm captain, and the beasts come at ten. Best to rest now.
{them}, I'm sleeping right here by the door. Wake me if anything scratches at the shutters.

{them}, a sellsword in the middle of the night, with bodies all around us. My name is {me}, of the city, and I'm captain of this guard. Are you looking for work, or for a way out of this house before the beasts come back?
{them}, the beasts come at ten. Stay close to the guards tonight, and let's settle the captain's vote at six tomorrow with a clear head.
{them}, I'm here to cast my vote for you. Your promise of guards and work for everyone is what I want to see.
{them}, good to see you at the hall. {mayor} has my vote, and I'd like to hear what you think of her plans for the town.
{mayor}, before the beasts come out, I want you to know I'm voting for you at noon. Get some rest, we have a town to keep.
{them}, keep quiet and stay put. We both need sleep before the vote.
{them}, you look like you haven't eaten either. Here, have an apple. I'm not asking for anything back, but if you hear of work, or who's hiring at the Lantern, let me know.
I'm not staying in the Wildwood with the sun going down. Back to the fields, I'm owed a shift.
{them}, stay quiet. The beasts are out, and this house is the safest place we have.
Bear! Guard, there's a bear at House 6!
Two apples in the pack, and the orchard's quiet. I'll eat one now and head back to the square before noon.
{them}, honest work is all I want. The Market square labour gang starts at eight and pays three coppers a shift. Come along and we'll see if they'll take us both.
{them}, keep an eye on the ovens while I see to the counter. Fresh bread for a copper, and I'll pay you fairly at close.
{them}, you look like you could use a bite. Bread's a copper at my counter, and the labour gang's still hiring if you need the coin.
{them}, I'll stay on through the afternoon. Is there bread I can take home for the night?
{them}, is there any work going, or a cheap bed for the night?
{them}, I'm hungry and I'm not going back to sleep on an empty stomach. Do you know where a cheap meal is at this hour?
Petra, the bakery's empty and I'm free until noon. Got any shifts left, or a loaf I can work for?
Ogre! Guard, help, there's an ogre in House 1!
Three coppers a day is more than I've had in a week, {them}. I'm {me}. Show me this labour post, and I'll be in the line before eight.
{them}, I'll finish the row before four. Then I'm going to the tavern for something hot and a drink, and I'll be paid for it.
Bear! Guard, over here, a bear is on {them}!
{them}, pull up a stool. The Lantern's the place to hear what's happening in this town, and the first round's on me.
{them}, you can keep your vote, but the ale's still on the bar. Serve the room for me till midnight and I'll pay you fair.
{them}, it's getting dark and the beasts come at ten. Get indoors, and if you're looking for work, come by the Lantern in the morning.
Poor souls. Let me see what they carried, then I'll take their things to the guard station so their people can be found.
Let me see what these two were carrying. Then I'm going to eat, and I'll be at the hall by noon for the vote.
{them}, I need hands in the Lantern and coin in both our pockets. Stay on, and we'll talk about the election after the rush.
{them}, I'm off to eat and then sleep. Keep the Lantern's door barred tonight, the beasts are out.
Enough of the Wildwood. I'm heading back to town before the beasts wake.
{them}, I'm thirsty and done in. I'll drink what I can and sleep. Good luck at noon.
Morning. Jailer's post, four coppers, and I'll keep my head down and get paid.
Water first, then back to the guard station before dark. I'm not sleeping in a house tonight.
{them}, the captain's said nothing to me but keep the cells locked and the bench quiet. I'll buy you a drink when we're paid. Don't go near the Lantern tonight on an empty purse.
{them}, I've got one copper and no ale to share, so we'll sit it out here. The beasts come at ten and the station's the strongest roof in town. Stay inside with me.
{them}, get inside and bar the door! Guard! Guard, there's a bear at House 3!
Night shift's coming. {mayor} keeps the guards paid, so I'll back her.
{them}, you want to know which doors open? Start with the one that pays a guard's wage and keeps you breathing after dark.
{them}, we're late. The Wildwood's no place to be after dark. Back to the square.
The chapel is empty and the Bear comes at ten. I'm going to the Drowned Lantern, where there are people.
Nobody sleeps in a house alone on a night like this. We're going to the market square, where the guards are, and I'll vote for {mayor} at noon.
Nobody's here, so I'll keep the chapel until ten and then get to the Drowned Lantern before the Bear comes out.
Chapel's quiet and the Bear comes at ten. I'm heading to the Drowned Lantern to be among people.
Ogre! {them}, run! Back to the town!

{them}, the labourers in this square get paid 3c a shift from eight. Work with me till four, then we shut ourselves indoors before ten. The Wildwood beast comes for whoever is out in the open, and it doesn't care whether they're asleep.
Evening, {them}. I'll take the floor till close.
{them}, I'll take whatever tables need clearing tonight.
The Wildwood is awake and it is hungry. Every coin you hoard is a bone it will count. Repent, and bar your doors before the bell strikes ten.
Hear me, sinners of Hollow Town: the Wildwood counts your coins as well as your sins. Tithe to the poor, shelter the stranger, and bar your doors before the bell.
The Wildwood keeps its own count, and it does not forget a hoarder. Shut your doors before the bell, and pray that your coins are not the reason it comes.
Morning. I'm {me}. Strong back, no trade, but I'll work honest. If anyone's hiring labour today, I'm your man.
A ranch hand or farmhand, {them}? That's the kind of honest work I'm after. Let's walk over to the ranch and the fields together, and see who's hiring before the sun gets much higher.
{them}, I'll be on my post at Market square tonight. Keep the pay coming and the guards fed, and you'll have my vote.
Water first, then I'll look for something to eat before I walk to the square for my watch.
An apple will have to do for now. Then I'll head into town for my watch.
{them}, {mayor}'s promised a guard on every street tonight. I'll be on the square at six, and I'll keep my eyes open.
{them}, I've wandered too deep in these woods with night coming. I'm heading back to the square for my watch.
Quiet out here tonight. {them}, keep your eyes on the lanes and your back to the wall.
{them}, I'm at my post. Anything you need from the jailer tonight?
Quiet morning at the station. I'll keep the cells in order and the books honest.
Captain, I'm thirsty and broke, but I'm keeping the cells in order. I'll back {mayor} and you, if the guard stays honest.
Mayor {them}, I'm one of your jailers and I'll keep the cells honest. Tell me where you need me before the vote.
Quiet at the station. I'll keep the cells in order until my shift ends.
{them}, I'm thirsty and broke, and I've kept the cells quiet all day. Anything you can tell me about the shift, or the captain's plans?
Work for anyone who'll take a guard's badge. Come and see me.
Anyone who doesn't want to sleep alone tonight, come to the square. The watch is there.
Well held, {them}. Get some rest when your watch is done.
It's paid, {them}, check your purse. Thank you, and I'll see you at noon.
The lanes stay lit, {them}, you have my word on it. See you at the count.
{them}, the Lantern is open. Hot ale and bread at fair prices, and I'm standing for mayor. Vote for the man who fills your belly.

{them}, you keep the town's books, so you know what the sales tax is doing to people. I'm standing for mayor tomorrow. Whatever I do with the Lantern, I'll keep the rolls honest and the bread cheap. Vote for me, and I'll see you're paid on time.
{them}, I respect that you'll vote your conscience. But the bread price is what matters to people here, and I'll keep it fair. Ask anyone who's eaten at the Lantern.
{them}, keep the hearth going and the ale flowing. Anyone who wants a bed off the street tonight, the Lantern's door is open. The Wildwood doesn't care who's asleep.
{them}, the Lantern's fire is staying lit tonight. Nobody goes out on Wick Lane alone when the Wildwood's awake.
{them}, who's that on the ground? Whatever's on them, I'll take it, since the Wildwood already did.
Nobody hunts in the Wildwood at noon with a boar on the path. I'm eating these grains and walking back to the Lantern before the beasts wake.
Morning, {them}. Let's keep the guard honest and the cells full of the right people.
{mayor} has kept this town standing. I'll vote for him and keep the cells honest.
{them}, keep your head down tonight. The beasts don't care whose house it is.
Stay inside tonight, {them}. I'll be at the guard station until ten, then I'm bolting my own door.
{them}, you're out foraging early too. Keep an eye out for the mayor's vote at noon.
Thank you, {them}. The clerk first, then I'll come find you. Your guard will want a man who can talk as well as he can stand watch.
{them}, I'm on the floor with you tonight. Keep the lanterns lit and the doors barred, and if anything comes out of the Wildwood, we shout together.
Morning, {them}. I survived the night, and I'm off to get bread before the election.
Mayor {them}, I'll keep my word. You'll have my vote at noon, and I'll be keeping the lanes lit with you. Hand over the coin.
{them}, the election's at noon. I'm off to the hall to keep my word to {mayor}.
Quiet morning at the station. I'll keep the cells honest and the coin counted.

{them}, I'd rather not sleep in a house tonight, not with the Wildwood hunting by scent. The guard station has walls and a lock. I'll meet you there at dusk, and we'll watch each other's backs until dawn.
Morning, all. I'm off for bread, then back to the cells before the Wildwood wakes.
Sounds good, {them}. Let's go. Two pairs of hands, and we'll split whatever honest work we find.
Morning. I run the general store now, so if you need bread, meal, or a shovel, come see me. Fair prices, and I'll keep the shelves stocked.
Still here at the counter. Bread, meal, eggs, turnips, fair prices.
Evening, {them}. Shop closes at six, so grab your bread before then. I'll be here till the last customer.
{them}, you awake? Stay close till dawn. We'll go to the town hall at noon and I'm voting {mayor}.
Honest work for honest coin. Let's keep this town standing.
Survive day three, you say? Then we'd better stick together and watch each other's backs. I'm {me}, I'm a guard, and I'd rather not be the one the Wildwood finds alone.
Captain's orders: nobody walks the lanes alone after dark. Meet at the guard station before the Wildwood wakes.
Guards, to the station now. Nobody sleeps alone tonight. We bar the doors and we keep each other awake until dawn.
{them}, wake up. The Wildwood wakes at dawn's dark hour, and we keep watch together. Eat an apple and stay close to me.
{them}, there's enough here for both of us. Let's gather what we can before the sun gets high.
Evening, {them}. I'm just in for a turnip and I'm not one to waste a doctor's time. If I take a knock tonight, I'll come to you first.
{them}, you wouldn't have a bit of work for a broke woman who knows her way around a ranch, would you?

Keep your head down and your coins close, {them}. Pay the clerk's office a visit when you can: the town hall keeps the lists, and a friendly face there hears about every opening before it's posted. Spend on bread and a bed first, and don't lend to anyone at the Drowned Lantern.
Good luck with the first shift, {them}. Keep your lantern lit and your head up.
Off to the town hall. Clerk's shift starts at nine, and I want to be there early.
Right on time for the clerk's desk. Let's get the ledgers in order.
Water first, then something to eat before the Wildwood wakes.
Water first, then the last apple. {them}, keep the door barred till the sun's up.
{them}, I'm still on Wick Lane until six. Keep your eyes on the beasts' road tonight, and let's both be behind a locked door by ten.
{them}, the beasts come at ten and they hunt by scent, so stay inside with me until dawn. You can owe me that favour once you're fed.
{them}, stay put until it's light. Then we'll find you something to eat.

{them}, you preach about the Wildwood, so you know it hunts by scent. Stay inside with me until it's light, and we'll get you something to eat at the bakery. A healer's favour is worth more than coin, so keep it in mind.
Bread first, then. Keep your favour in mind, {them}, and stay away from the Wildwood's road.
Good luck to you too, {them}. If you're walking the lane tonight, I'd rather be near your lantern than alone in here.
{them}, I'm hungry and I've got three coins. I'll take a turnip out of my wages and stay on the till until six.
{them}, I'm still on the till. Tell me if you want the shelves restocked before six.
{them}, I'll stay on the till until six. Then I'm heading home to bar the door before dark.
Morning, all. We made it through the night. {them}, I'm voting for you at noon. Let's find something to eat before the shops get their prices up again.
I'm barely standing, and I have two coins. I'll eat an apple and rest out of the way before I go anywhere.
I'll drink from the stream, eat one of these apples, and rest before the night shift. Nothing I'm taking off a corpse.
Morning, {them}. Busy day at the Smithy? I'm the new night guard, and I'd like to keep on the right side of the clerk's office. Any advice on how a coin goes furthest in this town?
Good advice, {them}. I'll stop by the town hall before my shift. Thank you.
Morning, all. I'm off to the town hall to see what openings there are before my shift.
{them}, I'm thirsty and off to the market for some bread before my shift.
Quiet night so far. I'll walk the lanes and keep my lantern up.
Morning. I'm the new doctor, and I'll be at the Infirmary if anyone needs tending.
Bear! Guards, over here! {them}, get back toward me, slowly!
I'm getting out of the Wildwood before dark. Anyone hurt on the road, come to the Infirmary.
{them}, I'm just waiting on the mayor's paperwork. Have you seen {mayor} around?
{mayor}, I'm with you. The guards are behind you, and I'll be on the lanes tonight.
Evening, {them}. Long shift. Are you heading to the lanterns tonight?
{them}, I'm bedding down here with you. Better two than one tonight.
Still here, {them}. Let's hold tight till dawn.
{them}, the lanes need a captain who keeps the guards together. I'll see the men fed and at their posts before dusk.
{them}, keep the lanterns lit and the men at their posts. We'll walk the lanes together before the bells.
Evening, all. I'm out of here before the Wildwood wakes.
{them}. You're awake before the dawn bell. Keep your voice down, the beasts can hear us through walls.
{them}, I heard nothing I'd repeat, and I'm not selling anyone's secrets for a promise. I'm sorry you were robbed. Find your coin some other way.
Someone should see to that body before it draws the rats. I'll take it to the morgue.
{them}, I'll take the morning's bodies and the paperwork. You keep the stiffs from the lane.
{them}, I'll eat first and be back before the shift ends. Keep the lamp lit.
Morning, {them}. Keep your lantern close tonight, and stay off the lanes after dark.
Thanks, {them}. Nobody sleeps alone tonight, and that includes you. Let's look after each other on the square.
{them}, I'll vote for you at noon. Keep your door barred tonight.
Keep your lamps lit, {them}. We'll see the sun up together.
{mayor}, you have my vote at noon. Keep the lanes lit.
Anyone about? I'm {me}, starting my server shift at four. I'd like to know who runs this place and what they pay.
{them}, I'm working the floor till midnight. Stay inside with us tonight, the Wildwood comes hunting at ten.
{them}, I'm sorry I missed the square yesterday. I'll make it up to you. Let's stay put until it's light, then go labour together.
{them}, keep quiet and keep your door barred. The Wildwood is coming.
Still inside. Doors barred. Let's all see the morning.
Still inside, bar the door. Quiet now.
Still inside. Barred and quiet.
Morning. Anyone need the chapel tended? I'll see to the sick.
{them}, the chapel is open if you need tending. Keep your head down till the Wildwood is quiet.
{them}, keep an eye on the lanes tonight. I'll be at the chapel till ten.
Quiet lane. Good. Keep walking the beat, and watch the shadows near the bakery.
{them}, steady on the square. Quiet afternoon, but the Wildwood won't stay quiet at night.
{them}, the Wildwood wakes at ten. Keep your lantern lit and stay near the guards.
Evening, all. {mayor} keeps the guard on the lanes, and that suits me. Let's get behind the doors before the Wildwood wakes.
Hear me, neighbours! The Wildwood is watching this town, and it counts every coin you hoard. Come to me, and I will show you how to be ready when it comes for us.
Keep your heads down and your hands busy, friends. The Wildwood is patient, but it will not forget what this town has done.
{them}, wake up. The Wildwood comes at ten, and it hunts by scent, even through walls. Stay close to me and keep your eyes on the door.
Quiet now, {them}. We survived the night, and I'll keep watch until the light comes.
Thank you, {them}. Keep your favour; I'll owe you one, and I'll remember it. Let's get bread before the market gets crowded.
{them}, you're a cleric, aren't you? I hear you keep the chapel and see to the sick. Is there any work in that for a guard with an empty purse?
Thank you, {them}. I'll look in at the Infirmary when the sick are bad. I'd rather earn my keep carrying water than sit idle with an empty purse.
{them}, I hear you're hunting work too. The fields pay little, but I'd rather be useful than idle until the night watch.
Quiet schoolhouse. I'll wait here a while and think on the town's coming election before my watch.
{them}, I'm off to the market square to take up my watch. Keep your head down tonight.
{them}, quiet here so far. Keep your eyes on the lanes until dawn.

{them}, you're the guard captain now? I'm {me}, a baker's hand. The sales tax is choking every household on this street. If the town wants honest workers, it needs wages that keep up with bread prices.
{mayor} has run this town on fear and fees long enough. I'm {me}, and I'll cut the sales tax and rent so folk can afford to eat.
{them}, you're on the ballot against me now. Let the town hear what you've done with its bread money. I'll be at the farm, and I'll be on the square at noon tomorrow to hear your answer.
{them}, I'm not here to beg, I'm here to be your replacement. I've got five coppers and a thirst, so I'll have a cup and think on what I'll do for this town.
{them}, it's past the hour the beast comes out. Get behind a barred door and stay there.
{them}, you're up before the Wildwood too. Stay in the house with us tonight, and let's keep each other alive until dawn.
{them}, that's sound thinking. I'll meet you at the guard station at dusk. Keep your lantern lit till then.
Morning, {them}. Bread's been scarce with this tax, but I need to eat before the next shift.
Quiet out here. I'll keep the market square on my watch until the shift ends.
Bread's still warm, {them}. A copper a loaf, and I'll take what I can get while the ovens are hot.
{them}, you're in my house tonight? I'll bar the door and keep my head down. Come noon, I'll see what your word is worth.
{them}, it's the middle of the night and the election's at noon. I'm keeping quiet and staying put.
{them}, keep the ovens hot. I'll take a loaf for my own belly and get back to the counter.
Morning. I'm {me}. I'll take honest work and keep my ears open.
{them}, is that you shouting? Hold on, I'll see what's wrong.
{them}, what's next on the rows?
That's the shift. Nobody left to talk to, so I'll head indoors before the beasts wake.
{them}, I'm awake and I've got a clear head now. Tell me plainly what you want from me, and what you'll pay for it.
{them}, the town's hiring guards. Pass the word.
To the square by ten, neighbours. Nobody sleeps alone tonight.
Bear! Bear in House 2! Guards!
Guards, we keep the peace and we all get home alive tonight. Watch the Wildwood edge after dark.
Good, {them}. Keep your eyes on the lanes and stay close to me. We'll see the town through until dawn.
Guards! Bear at House 2! Get the lanes closed and get {mayor} inside!
I've no coin and I'm hungry. Anything you can spare would help, friend.
I'm getting out of these woods before dark. Anyone heading for the town, I'd walk with you.
{them}, I'll tell you what I see, but I'd rather have coin than promises. Two coppers now, and I'll keep my eyes open for you.
{them}, keep the door barred. I'll stay right here till morning.
Morning, {them}. Whatever the Wildwood sends tonight, I'd rather not face it alone. Keep your door barred and stay where people are.
{them}, it's the middle of the night and the beasts are loose. Are you going to stand out here all night, or come inside with me?
Morning, {them}. One bread, if you'll take my last coin.
{them}, I'm short on coin and empty-handed. Is there more work at the forge before noon?
Beasts are out. I'm staying put behind this door and drinking my fill before I try to sleep.
Boars and deer everywhere. I'm not staying in these trees. Fish first, then back to the forge.
{mayor}'s in as mayor. I'll keep the forge going and get some food into me before dark.
Deer and rabbits, but I'm not hunting with the beasts due at ten. Berries first, then back to town before dark.
Beasts are still about, so we bar the door and sleep. {mayor} gets my vote at noon.
{them}! Get behind me! Bear, here!
Morning. Bread's fresh, and I'll work hard for a fair wage.
Parched already. I'll wet my throat, find something to eat, and be behind a bolted door before the Wildwood wakes.
{them}, I've no coin either, and I'm as hungry as you. The bakery's shut to me until morning, but I'll keep my eyes open for anything. Best we both get behind a bolted door before the Wildwood wakes.
Wrong place to be at this hour. Out of the trees and back to the bakery before the beasts wake.
Quiet now. I'll eat what I've foraged and bed down here with {them} and the others until morning.
{them}, keep the loaves coming. I'll take my shift and a bite when the rush thins.
{them}, the Lantern's door is open and the fire's still warm. Come inside before the lanes get worse.
Fenwick, I'll walk with you to the hall, but I'm not drinking on credit. {mayor} has my vote, and I'll come back to the Lantern to sell my grain.

{them}, I'm standing for mayor tomorrow, but I'm not running against anyone who keeps this town fed. Lower taxes and an honest wage for the people who work here. I'll be at the Lantern till midnight if you want to talk.
{them}, I'm staying here tonight. I'll vote for you at noon, and I'd rather be inside than on the lanes after dark.
{them}, I'll sleep here until light. I've got one coin, so I need the Lantern shift today.
I'm heading back to town now. {mayor}, I'm still voting for you at noon, and I'm not stopping here with the boars about.
{them}, I missed the vote at noon, so I'll be back for the next one. I'm heading to the Lantern for my shift, and I'd rather not be out after dark.
Nobody's here, so I'll bar the door and sleep. {mayor}, you have my vote at noon tomorrow.
Wildwood's no place to be after dark. I need coin and a bed indoors.
Sales tax at fifty percent? Hard to keep a purse full with that.
Bear! Guard, {mayor}'s down out there!
{them}, we're not staying in the Wildwood. Catch what you can quickly, then we get to the smithy for a club and home before dark.
{them}, good evening. I'm {me}, of the city's minor nobility, and I'm standing for mayor. The town hall takes the five-coin fee, I believe? I'd value your word on how the ballot is kept.
Bear! Guard, over here! {mayor}'s down!
Terrible night. Whoever is left standing, we need a mayor who can keep the lanes safe. I'm running, and I'll pay the fee now.
{them}, I'm {me}, standing for mayor at noon. Hollow Town needs a smithy that works, and so do the guards. Any work you can spare for a sellsword?
Pupils, I'll see you tomorrow. Stay safe until nightfall, and keep your doors barred.
Enough foraging. I need to get back to town before the beasts come out.
Bear! Guard, there's a bear on {them}, over here!

Honestly, {them}? Not well. We walk the lanes with torches and lanterns, and we bang on doors at dusk so folk get indoors before ten. Beyond that, we're mostly counting on people being smart and staying behind shuttered windows. Why do you ask? Are you thinking of signing on?
{them}, there's a body out here. Let's see who it was before the beasts come back.
{them}, bolt the door. We stay in until the Bear is gone.
Let's get the first patients seen before the day runs away from us.
{them}, good day to you too. If anyone's carried in tonight, I'll have the bandages ready and I'll see them stabilised before they reach your cells. Keep the door barred and your own skin whole.
Eat something hot, then get indoors before ten.
{them}, I'd take that meal gladly, and I'll stay inside with you until morning. I'm not a fighter, but I can stitch and stabilise anyone who's hurt.
{them}, it's too late to be out. Let's stay inside here together until the Wildwood settles.
Dawn's nearly here and I've survived the night. Let's get food into everyone before the next dark.
{them}, I need honest work before the beasts come. Is there a shift I can take beside you?
Nobody out here but the beasts. I'm going to keep quiet and find a corner to hide in.
Five berries and an empty purse won't see me through the ogre's night. Who's hiring before the beasts come?
{mayor}, I'm voting for you at noon. Tonight is the ogre's night, so I'm going somewhere with a bolted door.
{them}, I'll take any honest shift you've got before the beasts come. I'm a sellsword with no coin and no food.
Ogre! Guard, get the guard, there's an ogre at House 5!
Just a quick bite, then I'm home to bar the door before the bell.
Too late for shopping. Home, and bar the door.
{them}, I'll take a bite of something quick. Then I'm home before the bell.
{them}, I need coin before the Wildwood wakes. I'll find honest work today and be home before dark.
Pool what we have, {them}? I've got nothing in my purse but lint. Still, one roof is the right call. I'll be home before ten, and we'll bar the door together.
I won't take a fight I can't walk away from, {them}. You have my word. Bar the door, and I'll be home before the bell.
{them}, I'm home before the bell, and the door's barred behind us. Let's get through the night.
{them}, any work at the bakery this afternoon? I'll carry sacks for bread.
Get off her! Ogre, turn on me!
Morning. Whatever the town needs, I'll be at the ranch working hard today.
Long day. I'll eat, drink, and stay indoors tonight.
Hollow Town deserves honest guards, not crooks in gilded coats. I'll earn my coin with my sword and my word.
{them}, you're a night guard, aren't you? I'm {me}. I hear the Wildwood beasts come hunting at ten. How do you keep the lanes safe with only a handful of you?
Not well enough, then. Thank you for being honest, {them}. If I get the captaincy, I'll give you real lanterns and real men on every lane, and nobody will be left to bang on doors alone.
Bear! Guard, get down to House 6! Someone light a lantern!
{them}, I'm standing for mayor today. Real guards, lit lanes, and no more people left to the beasts. Will you hear me out?
{mayor} won the vote, so I'll take honest work until the next election. Hollow Town will need every willing pair of hands before the beasts come again.
{them}, I'll take a server's shift at the Lantern tonight. Honest coin, and I'll be inside before the beasts come.
Mayor {mayor}, the chapel will need hands before the beasts wake. I'm here to help.
Night's coming. I'll stay here at the chapel where the lamps are lit.
Bear! {them}, get back from the door! Guard, over here!
Nine meat and a bearpelt. I'll trade them fair, and I'll vote for {mayor} at noon.
{mayor} has the town's ear for now. I'll be watching who keeps the lanes safe tonight.
{them}, you work the bakery's early shift. Tell me who in this town eats well and who goes hungry, and I'll make sure you're one of the ones who eats.
Friends, I'm standing for mayor at noon. Keep the lanes lit, keep the guard paid, and I'll keep the beasts off your doorsteps.
Drinks are on me at the Lantern tonight. Tomorrow at noon, vote for the one who lowered your taxes.
{them}, you're a sharp one. Stand against me if you like, but the lanes are safer with a mayor who knows them. Come work with me and you'll eat well.
Stay in the Lantern tonight, where there's company and a door that bars. Vote for me at noon and you'll keep your coin.
I've got three apples and a coin, so I'll eat first and then buy bread. Who's heading to the town hall for the vote at noon?
{mayor}, congratulations on the win. I'm the town clerk, and I'm looking for honest work before the beasts come out tonight. Is there a post left to fill?
Mayor {mayor}, I'm the town clerk and I'll vote for you tomorrow. Rent has dropped to 2c, so I can manage a bed if I can find work today. Is there any post left I can fill before dark?
{mayor}, I'll be at the hall tomorrow noon to see the count is fair. Tonight I'll be indoors before the ogre comes.
Evening, everyone. I'm still looking for work before the ogre comes tonight. Anyone who needs a hand, I'm your man.
{mayor}, I'm still captain and I'll keep the guard on its feet. Lower the rent and I'll back you at the vote.

{them}, the guard isn't hiring coin-for-coin right now, but I'll take a smith's help at the gate tonight. Come by the lanterns before ten and bring your wits. If the bounty board pays for beast hides, I'll see you're paid for them.
{them}, keep watch by the door. I'll stay put until the lanterns come back up.
{them}, the dead are still out here. Let's get the bodies seen to before the square fills up.
Evening. Any work going for a man with sharp eyes?
Bear! Guards, get the guard!
{them}, I'll keep my door barred and my feet away from the Wildwood's edge. Come to me tonight if you must, but bring a prayer with you. The beasts will not hear our bargaining.
{them}, you're here. Stay close to me and say your prayers. We'll wait out the night together.
{mayor} is the sitting mayor now, and she has my vote. Lower rent and a curfew sound wise with the beasts coming. I'll work the shift and keep my wits about me tonight.
{them}, I've no coin to spare tonight, but I'll pray for your safe return. The beasts come at ten; I'm barring my door.
{them}, I've got an apple and a few coins. We'll share what we have and keep the door barred until the beasts pass.
{them}, the town needs guards before ten tonight, and the pay is 4c a day. Take a badge and give me your vote at noon tomorrow, and there's 2 coppers in it for you now.
Spears and shields at the smithy, cheap, today only. The ogre comes on the last night.
Bear! {them}'s down, get out of the trees! Guard!
Everyone, out the back and away from that bear! Head for the houses, quick!
{them}, has anyone at the Lantern heard what {mayor} plans for the guards? I'd rather hear it from you than from the bear.
{them}, I'm off to House 4 before the beasts wake. Keep your head down tonight.
{them}, get out of the Wildwood before the boar notices us. Town first, then we eat.
Bear! Everyone, out the far door and keep moving. Don't run in the open, make for the houses!
{them}, I've had nothing to eat since the Wildwood and no coin to my name. Could you spare a crust? I'll make it right when the town pays.
{them}, a few more hours and the shift is done. Then we all go indoors before the Wildwood wakes.
{them}, the bell's nearly rung. Then water, then food, then indoors before the Wildwood wakes.
{them}, I'm hungry and I've got a fish. Is there a bed in the jail tonight, somewhere with a roof and a door?
Thank you, {them}. Keep your fish. I'll find work at the chapel and a bite before the day's out.
I've got no coin and an empty pack, so I'll earn my bread at the chapel and fish the stream after.
Fed for now. I'll keep the shift at the chapel until seven, then the Wildwood can find me indoors.
{them}, one more hour of this and then I'm going straight home to bar the door. The Wildwood won't find me in a locked house.
Ogre! Guards, the Wildwood's at House 3 with {them}!
{them}, I'm listening. I want food and water first, then we'll talk about who runs this place.
I've got one coin and an empty belly. Anyone spare a scrap of bread for a guard who's been on the lanes?
Two coins, and I'm starving. {them}, I'll take a meal and keep my eyes on the lanes for you.
{mayor}, a meal for my two coins. Then I'm off to bar a door before the beasts wake.
{them}, I've got no work to hand out tonight, and the beasts wake soon. Find a barred door and stay off the lanes.
Ogre! Out the back, everyone, now!
Quiet in here. I'll eat what I have and rest until the election.
I'll eat an apple, then get back to town before noon. The vote's at the hall, and I need paid work.
Evening. I'm on the night guard tonight, and I'll eat before the lanes.
Night guard reporting for the shift. Lanes are mine until six.
Guard! Boar, {them}! Somebody get the guard, he's being attacked in the Wildwood!
Night guard here. Who's with me on the square? Stay in a group, and keep your backs to a wall.
{them}, get out of these woods now. The ogre comes tonight, and I'm going to the chapel to work until it's safe indoors.
{them}, I'm staying at the chapel until the shift ends. The ogre comes tonight, so this is the safest place I know.
{them}, I'm bolting the door and staying put until morning. Keep your voice down.
{them}, the ogre comes at ten. Bar the door and keep quiet. I'm eating my fish and sleeping here.
{them}, get inside now. The ogre comes on the last night. Bar your door.
Quiet out here. I'll stay by the lamps and watch the square until the bell.
{them}, I'm not staying out here in the Wildwood by daylight. I'm eating this fish and going back to the square before the vote.
Bear! Guards, here at House 1!
{them}, I've no coin to hire anyone tonight, but I know the guard rota and who's looking for hands. Come to the Drowned Lantern with me; we'll find you something before the beasts come out.
Anyone with a spare hour's labour, I'm here. I can haul, mind a stall, or walk the lanes for a fair wage.
{them}, I'll take the afternoon row. I want my 3c and something to eat tonight.
{them}, I've got a jailer's post at the guard station now. Keep your head down and get home before dark.

{them}, you're a sellsword, so you know the trade. The town is paying guards 4c a day at the station, and I'd rather see you on the right side of the law than hiring out to the wrong crowd. Stay honest and we'll both sleep easier.
Quiet shift at the station. I'll keep the cells tidy and get home before the beasts come out.
Mayor {mayor}, congratulations. I'm owed my clerk wages from yesterday, and I need food before the beasts come out. Can the 200% sales tax come down as you promised?
Mayor {them}, I still haven't been paid my 3c clerk wages from yesterday, and I have nothing to eat. Can I keep the desk and be paid today?
{them}, I'm {me}, the town clerk. I'm hungry and I have no coin, and I hear the town is hiring. Is there any work I can do for you tonight?
Mayor {them}, the sales tax is down to 25% and rent to 1c, so thank you. I'm still hungry and broke. Can I have that server shift at the Drowned Lantern tonight, or any work at all?
{mayor} keeps the lanes safer and the taxes lower. Vote for him.
{them}, keep your fish. A jail cell is a cell, not a bed, and I'm not locking up a friend. But if you're hungry, let's split what we have and find you a roof before the beasts come.
{them}, we're both alive. Stay low, bar the door, and we'll see the sun together. I'm heading for the square at dawn.
Morning, {them}. I'm hungry and I've got 4c, so I'll buy bread and get some rest before the vote.
{mayor}, one ale for me, and I'll pay what I can. I'm on the square at ten and I'm not leaving my post tonight.
I'm late for the square, but I'm going now. Tonight is the ogre's night, so we stand together.
{them}, I'm back on the cows. Keep the shifts coming, and I'll keep my hands honest.
Out of the Wildwood before the bell. Fish first, then the lamps of the Lantern.
No food and no coin. I need a shift before the light goes, and then I'll ask for bread.
{them}, I've got no coin and no supper. Any shift left at the ranch, or a crust from the market?
No roof of my own and no coin. The Lantern has the crew and a fire. I'll stay with them until the beasts are done.
Quiet hour. I'll slip into a house for coin and food, then find a hidden corner to sleep before the beasts wake.
Evening, Captain. {me} reporting for the night watch. Keep your eyes on the lanes and your doors barred.
A poor traveller from the city, friends, hungry and far from home. Any kindness would be remembered.
{them}, good morning. {me}, of the city. Has the night been kind to you? Mine was long, and I'm famished.
Innkeeper, a hot meal and a cup of ale for a gentleman of the city. I'll settle the account after my shift.
{them}, you look like a man who has seen better days, as I have. Walk with me to the tavern. A well-connected friend is worth more than coin, and I know who to talk to.
{them}, thanks for the bed. I'm going to the fields for the morning shift, then I'll vote at noon.
{them}, I'm still on the row. Is there any pay left for today, or a bit of work before dusk?
{them}, I'm out of coin, so I'll stay here with you tonight. Let's keep the door shut.
{them}, I'm not here to fight. I'm going to see what these folk left behind, then I'm getting indoors before dawn.
{mayor} won the vote, so let's see what honest work the new mayor offers. I'll take sellsword shifts here until dusk.
Nobody here to hire me, so I'll get some food and head to the Market square before the beasts come.
Friend, I'm hungry and I've got one coin. Anything you can spare?
Nobody's about. I'll keep to the square and wait for the guards.
{them}, I'm going to eat these fish and then find sellsword work before the beasts come out tonight.
{them}, I'm {me}, a sellsword with one coin and a strong arm. If the town needs guards, I'm your man.
Nobody about this early. I'll drink, look for food in the hedgerows, then get to the Market square before the beasts come out.
{them}, I'm bolting this door and staying put till dawn.
Morning. I'm on the fields until four, so let's get the turnips and eggs in before the heat.
{them}, good timing. The farm's short a hand until four. Help me finish these turnips and I'll split the pay with you.
Nobody's about, so I'll keep my head down. I'm eating my last berry and sleeping until the farm shift.
{them}, wake up. Let's get something hot to eat, and then I need hands on the farm until four.
{them}, the only name on the ballot is yours. Take it if you want it, and I'll back you at noon. Right now I'm drinking water and sleeping until the farm shift.

{them}, I won the vote, so I'm the mayor now, and I'm not taking your 2c. But you're right that the town needs guards. Stand with me and I'll give you a guard's post at 4c a day, paid from the town purse. We both get out of the Wildwood before dark.
Everyone, get indoors before 22:00. The Wildwood is coming, and the guard will walk the streets tonight.
{them}, get inside before dark. I'll see the guard walks the square tonight.
{them}, you're on the ballot too, and I respect that. Pour me an ale on credit if you can. Everyone, the beasts come at ten, so bar your doors.
{them}, it's the small hours. I'll rest here a while, then head for the bakery.
I'll eat these berries now, then get bread and be at the hall for the vote.
{mayor} won the seat, so I'll work for the town and keep my head down. {them}, if you're hungry too, the Infirmary needs hands.
I'm the doctor here. If anyone's hurt or sick, come to the Infirmary and I'll see you before the beasts come out.
The beasts are out. I'll stay inside the Infirmary with whoever's here until morning.
{them}, I'm going to the tavern for a meal, then I'm looking for paid work before the beasts come out.
I'm wounded and hungry, but I'm on duty at the infirmary. Someone needs to tend the sick before the beasts come.
I'm still weak, but I'll eat and get back to the infirmary. Piers, {mayor} has my vote.
I'll keep the infirmary open until my shift ends, then bar the doors. Whatever comes tonight, I'm not going out into the Wildwood.
The ogre is gone and so is the night. I need food and water before I think about the vote.

{them}, I've got no coin to spare and the ranch pays only 3c a shift, but I'll not turn a hungry man away. Come to the ranch before the morning shift and we'll see what work there is. Stay out of the Wildwood.
The ranch needs tending before the election. I'll see the animals fed and the fences checked.
Bear! Everyone out of House 1, get clear of it!
The ogre comes at ten tonight. Everyone get indoors and bar your doors.

{them}, you look like you've been walking the fields since dawn with nothing to show for it. I'm a night guard, I have no coin and no spare work to offer, but if you want a steady shift the town hall is where the jobs and the election are decided. Keep your head down near the Wildwood after dark.
Keep the lanes covered and the beasts off the streets. Guards, report to your posts, and nobody is out in the Wildwood after dark.
Drink up, lock the doors, and nobody goes near the Wildwood tonight.
{them}, we're both night guards now. Mind the lanes with me tonight, and we'll sort the rest after.
{them}, I'm for the night watch and I'm off to eat before the beasts come out at ten. Keep your wits about you.
Bear! Guards, help, it's at House 1!
{them}, I'm {me}. I've got one copper and no job yet, so I can't pay you, but I'll share whatever work we find. Let's look for something honest together.
Morning. I'm {me}. I'm new here and broke, but I work hard and keep my word. Who's hiring?
Anyone here? I'm {me}, and I'm ready to work the counter.
Two apples will do for now. Tomorrow I'll work the counter and find some coin.
{them}, I'm {me}. I've got two good hands and a fish in my pack. Need a day's work on the fields? I'll take a fair wage, and I'll keep the Lantern shift in mind.
{them}, I'm off to the Lantern for my server's shift. If you hear of work, I'll be there.
{them}, one more round and then I'm on the floor until midnight. Barred doors tonight.
I'll eat this fish and head to the Lantern for my shift. Nobody should be alone tonight.

Morning, {them}. Word is the Wildwood beasts come out at ten every night and nobody's safe in their beds. And the mayor's seat is open for the taking come noon tomorrow. Three coins is a start, but I'd rather we find work together than wait on the town to hand it out.
{them}, you're up early, and you look like you haven't slept. Are we going to find work today, or are we going to stand here watching the others get the good jobs?
Then stop standing here and go. Take the first job that will have you, and I'll do the same. We can't afford to be last.
